suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin/Theme Backdoor Installation via File Write
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Exposed Hacker Server Reveals WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites'—backdooring implies malicious plugin/theme injection as persistence vector. No execution-phase UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /wp-content/plugins/ and /wp-content/themes/ for suspicious PHP file creation/modification outside of WP admin upload processes. Alert when: (1) files are written by non-web-server accounts, (2) timestamps cluster around vulnerability exploitation, or (3) created files call eval(), base64_decode(), or exec() without corresponding legitimate plugin manifests.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Execution via PHP Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Malware named 'SHELLSTORM' implies shell/web shell payloads. Title mentions 'exposed hacker server'—web shells provide remote code execution and persistence. No execution-phase detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes spawning unusual child processes (bash, sh, curl, wget, nc) without corresponding application context. Alert on proc_open/shell_exec/system/passthru calls with command-line arguments matching shell metacharacters, pipes, or process substitution (e.g., `whoami | nc`). Baseline legitimate WP Cron and plugin execution.

suggestion.title: Backdoor Command and Control Communication from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'exposed hacker server'—implies attacker C2 infrastructure. Thousands of compromised sites require ongoing command channel. No C2 detection UC was created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound HTTP POST/GET requests from httpd/nginx processes to untrusted/dynamically-registered domains, especially with encoded payloads in request body, atypical User-Agent headers (curl variants, no UA), or connections to known C2 registrars. Correlate with periodic/regular timing (beaconing).

suggestion.title: Suspicious WordPress Core File Tampering (wp-config, wp-settings, index.php)
suggestion.rationale: Persistence on thousands of sites requires modification of WordPress bootstrap files. Article does not detail specific files, but backdoor implants modify core files. No file-integrity UC exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to wp-config.php, wp-settings.php, wp-load.php, index.php, and .htaccess in WordPress root/subdirectories. Alert if: (1) modification occurs outside maintenance windows, (2) file hash differs from WordPress version baseline, (3) file contains obfuscated PHP (base64, gzinflate, eval), or (4) ownership/permissions change unexpectedly.

suggestion.title: WP-SHELLSTORM Malware Hash and Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly names threat: 'WP-SHELLSTORM'. No hash-based or YARA-rule detection UC was generated despite named malware family presence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create file-hash and behavioral detections for known WP-SHELLSTORM samples. Monitor for staging directories, obfuscated PHP payloads with common backdoor patterns (base64-encoded PHP, gzinflate, @eval), and unusual plugin/theme naming. Alert on YARA matches for WordPress-specific persistence signatures.

suggestion.title: Anomalous WordPress Admin Account Creation or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor persistence implies attacker maintains administrative access for command execution. Article does not specify but account enumeration/creation is standard post-compromise. No credential-access UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WordPress user table modification (wp_users INSERT/UPDATE), wp-cli account creation commands executed by web processes, or database queries creating admin-level roles outside business hours. Alert on bulk user creation, accounts with suspicious naming (admin2, backup_user, sys_admin), or role escalation without corresponding UI audit logs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Redirection to Orphaned Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' and 'The attacker re-pointed several existing release tags to their malicious commit.' This is tagset manipulation—detecting tag movements to non-branch commits is critical for supply-chain defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for tag creation, deletion, or reference updates. Alert when a tag is moved to a commit hash not reachable from main/master/develop branches, or when existing semantic version tags (v* pattern) are reassigned to orphaned commits outside normal release workflow. Correlate tag changes with unusual commit authorship.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Changing existing release tags to point to the attack commit. Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch.' Orphaned commits are forensically visible but behaviorally suspicious—they lack branch association yet remain accessible via commit hash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commit creation where the commit is never pushed to any named branch but is immediately referenced in a tag. Flag when commit reachability queries show zero branch associations despite tag existence. High signal when repo has <5 active branches and orphaned commits exceed historical baseline.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Exposed in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An attacker with write privileges on the Action repo made a commit that caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' and 'GitHub has a sophisticated encryption scheme for managing secrets... without the secret ever appearing in the build log.' This is the direct impact—detecting plaintext secrets in action logs is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest GitHub Actions run logs and scan for patterns matching AWS_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT, Snyk tokens, or base64-encoded secrets matching known encryption algorithms. Alert on plaintext secret exposure in publicly visible logs. Cross-reference with repo's declared secret names to identify injection points.

suggestion.title: External Network Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' External C2 calls from GitHub infrastructure are high-fidelity supply-chain indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS and network flow logs for outbound connections initiated from GitHub Actions runners. Flag domains that are not whitelisted GitHub/npm/package registry hosts. Correlate external calls with modified workflows or newly updated Actions. Alert on C2 domains known to host malware payloads (cross-check threat feeds).

suggestion.title: Write Access Granted to High-Dependency GitHub Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'As of this writing, it's unknown why the attacker had write permissions on the repo that houses this GitHub Action code.' and 'The bottom line is that a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Detecting new or suspicious write-access grants to widely-used shared repos is early warning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new collaborator additions with write/admin permissions to public repos with >1000 downstream dependencies. Flag if adding user lacks commit history in past 6 months, uses newly created account, or IP geolocation diverges from repo's active contributors. Cross-reference with phishing/account compromise alerts.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Dependency Pinning Bypass via Tag Redirection
suggestion.rationale: Article illustrates how developers trust semantic version tags: 'If we're told to use v35 of a particular release, we reference that tag and assume that's what we'll be getting.' Attacker exploited this by moving v35 tag. Detect when pinned Action versions diverge from expected commit hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a manifest of expected commit hashes for each pinned GitHub Action version across organization. Monitor workflow executions and compare resolved commit hash against manifest. Alert when 'uses: org/action@v35' resolves to an unexpected commit, especially if commit is orphaned or authored by non-standard contributor.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Scanner - CVE-2023-4346 Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4346 and CISA KEV status means active exploitation observed. Pipeline must baseline all KNX devices on network and flag those missing the patch before federal due date 2026-07-29.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt vulnerability scanners and asset-management systems for KNX Association products running KNX Protocol versions vulnerable to CVE-2023-4346. Correlate patch-missing assets against network segment ownership to identify exposure.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Asset Inventory - Unauthenticated Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options'—implies attacker discovers devices first via unauthenticated KNX protocol enumeration or weak auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans targeting KNX standard ports (3671 TCP/UDP) from external or lateral-movement sources. Flag any KNX device enumeration without device-owner approval or known asset-inventory tools.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Device Lock/BCU Key Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker ability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—this is an admin-level configuration change on a critical industrial device. Should trigger on any BCU modification outside change-control windows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device management interfaces and gateway audit logs for BCU key changes, device lock commands, or credential resets originating from non-whitelisted admin accounts or external IPs. Correlate with failed auth attempts on preceding logs.

suggestion.title: Bulk Device Purge / Factory Reset Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'purge all devices'—this is a batch destructive operation. Single or multiple factory resets in short timeframe is anomalous and maps to impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device reset/purge commands sent to multiple KNX devices in a single session or short time window. Baseline expected maintenance resets by geography/owner; flag any reset storms outside change-control approval.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Weak-Auth KNX Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Connection Authorization Option 1' is overly restrictive—implies attacker can bypass or ignore auth entirely. Should detect any KNX traffic from unknown sources or without expected TLS/credential headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX protocol traffic (port 3671) originating from external networks or non-managed segments without valid device credentials. Flag any plaintext KNX handshakes or failed auth followed by device configuration commands.

suggestion.title: KNX Connection Authorization Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Connection Authorization Option 1 contains an overly restrictive account lockout mechanism vulnerability'—direct evidence of CVE-2023-4346 exploitation targeting the authorization layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol traffic (default ports 3671 UDP/TCP) for malformed Connection Authorization frames, repeated failed auth attempts targeting Option 1 mechanism, or authentication bypass indicators. Correlate with any successful device access lacking valid credentials.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized BCU Key Lockout Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'can set a BCU key to lock the device'—post-exploitation indicator of successful vulnerability abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BCU key creation or modification events outside maintenance windows, especially device-locking keys set by non-administrative accounts or unexpected source IPs. Flag rapid sequential BCU key changes across multiple devices.

suggestion.title: Mass KNX Device Purge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—bulk device erasure is the primary denial-of-service impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on device purge commands affecting >N devices in <5min window, especially from non-administrative sources or accounts without historical device reset privileges. Correlate with lockout mechanism abuse in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Account Lockout Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability directly exploits the account lockout mechanism ('overly restrictive')—abuse of this mechanism is the exploitation vector itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal account lockout patterns per KNX device. Flag spikes in lockout events from single sources, repeated lockout-and-unlock cycles suggesting mechanism probing, or lockouts followed by successful authentication to the same device within seconds.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Inventory Exposure Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation requires federal agencies remediate by due date 2026-07-29; standard asset-exposure hunt needed to identify CVE-2023-4346-vulnerable devices in your environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all KNX-enabled devices via network scanning (port 3671), query asset database for KNX products from vulnerable versions, cross-reference with patch management system. Flag any unpatched devices exposed to untrusted networks or internet-accessible control interfaces.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Vulnerability Scanner Match — CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and mandates federal patch due 2026-07-29. Canonical asset-exposure hunt per template reference.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for KNX devices with CVE-2023-4346 or running 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1'. Alert on unpatched instances; correlate with patch compliance timelines for federal audit readiness.

suggestion.title: KNX Mass Device Lockout Spike
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability permits attacker to 'set a BCU key to lock the device' — attack directly locks devices. Should detect multi-device lockout bursts indicating mass exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal BCU key configuration changes and device lockout state transitions. Alert when 5+ devices enter locked state from same source IP/account within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge Operation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled' — direct device wipe capability. Detect bulk purge commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate KNX device purge operations. Alert on sequential mass purge commands (10+ commands within 1 minute) or purges initiated from unexpected accounts/IPs.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE roots in 'Connection Authorization Option 1' — protocol-level attack vector. Network signatures should detect malformed handshakes or authorization bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol traffic for malformed 'Connection Authorization' frames, unusual authentication sequences, or protocol violations. Alert on repeated failed authorization attempts followed by successful device manipulation commands.

suggestion.title: VPN App Traffic Not Encrypted—Cleartext Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states apps exhibit 'unencrypted data' as primary finding. Detection must surface VPN applications sending network traffic via HTTP instead of HTTPS, or cleartext protocols.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Android VPN app processes for unencrypted outbound connections (HTTP, telnet, FTP). Baseline: VPN apps should encrypt >95% of traffic. Flag VPN app destination IPs using cleartext protocols; correlate with known tracking domain IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Tracking Beacon Exfiltration from VPN App
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents 'tracking' as core vulnerability—apps send user data to third-party analytics/ad networks without consent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN app processes connecting to ad/analytics networks (Facebook, Google Analytics, AppsFlyer, Adjust, Mixpanel). Flag if DNS resolution reveals VPN app querying advertising domains. Alert on data exfiltration patterns in packet inspection (embedded IMEI, email, phone numbers).

suggestion.title: DNS Leak from VPN App—Unrouted Queries
suggestion.rationale: Traffic leak finding implies DNS resolution bypasses the VPN, exposing user browsing intent. Article states apps fail to properly tunnel all traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries originating from Android devices using free VPN apps. Flag if queries resolve to ISP nameservers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, OpenDNS) instead of VPN provider's DNS. Baseline: all DNS traffic should tunnel through VPN provider infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Excessive Permissions Granted to VPN App
suggestion.rationale: Free VPN apps with data leakage typically request location, microphone, camera, contacts beyond network requirements—article implies apps access data beyond encryption scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN application permission grants for camera, microphone, location, contacts, SMS, call logs. Correlate permission grants with subsequent network exfiltration to non-VPN IPs. Alert on VPN apps requesting runtime permissions after install.

suggestion.title: VPN App Proxy Interception—SSL Stripping Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Unencrypted data finding suggests apps may proxy user traffic and strip TLS—active MITM rather than misconfiguration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN app processes capturing inbound HTTPS traffic and forwarding as cleartext HTTP. Look for certificate pinning bypass signatures, SSL version downgrade requests, or HTTP traffic on port 443. Monitor for VPN app installing unauthorized root certificates.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via VPN App—Structured PII in Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Article describes VPN apps leaking 'data'—detection must identify PII, credentials, or device identifiers embedded in network requests sent by the app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect network traffic from VPN app for patterns matching email addresses, phone numbers, IMEI, Android ID, location coordinates, or device serial numbers in HTTP query parameters or POST bodies. Flag bulk data transfers to IPs outside VPN provider's infrastructure. Consider YARA rules for embedded tracking SDK signatures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs: 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2023-4346; federal patch due 2026-07-29. Pipeline produced empty IOCs despite this high-priority CISA KEV scanning indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner outputs for CVE-2023-4346 detections on KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 instances. Correlate pre-patch-deadline asset inventory snapshots. Flag any devices still vulnerable post-2026-07-29 deadline to measure remediation slippage.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing KNX Device Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets)' and directs to asset-exposure template hunt. Pipeline generated no detection logic despite explicit guidance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX devices reachable from Internet using network asset discovery (port 3671/tcp characteristic of KNX-IP). Cross-reference internal inventory with external exposure databases. Flag any internet-routable KNX instances and escalate for network isolation or firewall hardening.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Purge and BCU Key Lockout
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker capability: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device.' Pipeline missed this clear impact-phase detection opportunity despite explicit attack description.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device management and audit logs for unauthorized device erasure commands, firmware resets, or BCU (Backbone Coupler Unit) key modifications. Alert on bulk device state changes within narrow timeframes. Correlate with authentication failures or credential-compromise signals.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: CVE specifically targets 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism.' Attackers exploit this to lock out administrators or themselves persist. Article implies this as exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential failed authentication attempts against KNX devices, especially administrative accounts. Flag accounts locked immediately after unauthorized access probes. Correlate with known CVE-2023-4346 exploitation timeframes.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Anomalous Command Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker actions post-compromise: 'purge all devices' and 'set a BCU key.' Pipeline missed protocol-level execution detection for these device-manipulation commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol traffic for anomalous command patterns: mass device reset sequences, BCU key write operations, or administrative commands from unexpected source addresses. Baseline legitimate device-management traffic and alert on deviations during business-hour peaks.

suggestion.title: Exposed KNX Devices on Internet-Facing Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article flags T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' as the attack vector; CVE-2023-4346 exploitation requires network reachability. Article body explicitly states vulnerability is in public-facing context. Detect KNX devices exposed on routable networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization devices accessible from untrusted networks. Monitor for inbound connections to KNX ports (3671/tcp, 3671/udp). Cross-reference vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2023-4346 against network reachability assessments.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2023-4346)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'Connection Authorization Option 1 lockout mechanism'; this is exploited via malformed protocol frames. Detect failed authorization attempts and exploitation payloads targeting the CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IDS signatures detecting KNX protocol malformations or CVE-2023-4346 exploit patterns. Monitor for repeated failed KNX authorization attempts from single source followed by state-change commands. Flag unexpected protocol behavior (e.g., out-of-sequence lockout mechanism triggers).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Mass Device Purge / Reset (KNX Impact)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could purge all devices without additional security options enabled'; this is the concrete impact. Detect unexpected batch device state resets or data wipes across KNX infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX gateway logs and protocol captures for group/broadcast commands triggering device memory clear or reset operations. Alert on unexplained mass device state transitions. Correlate with failed device heartbeats or management interface access anomalies.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Compromise or Unauthorized Device Lock
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker 'could set a BCU key to lock the device'; BCU (Backbone Coupler Unit) key write is device credential compromise and lock-out. Detect unauthorized BCU key manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX protocol frames writing to BCU key material or triggering device-lock operations. Alert on unexpected changes to device security state. Correlate with failed downstream authentication attempts on locked devices.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Standard CISA KEV baseline control; federal patch due 2026-07-29. Mandatory vulnerability scan detection and asset tracking for unpatched KNX Connection Authorization Option 1 instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2023-4346 against known KNX Association product instances. Alert on any unpatched or unknown-version devices. Track remediation status against federal due date of 2026-07-29.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and references canonical template with this CVE as the substitution target. Zero use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all systems detected as vulnerable to CVE-2023-4346 (KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1) in vulnerability scanners. Prioritize exposed KNX devices on internet-facing or untrusted network segments given CISA KEV status (active exploitation).

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Service Reconnaissance / Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain requires discovering KNX installations first. Article describes 'purge all devices' implying network enumeration phase. No reconnaissance detection included.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scans or service enumeration targeting known KNX protocol ports. Correlate failed KNX service discovery attempts followed by successful connections or authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Device Configuration / BCU Key Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'set a BCU key to lock the device' and 'purge all devices without additional security options.' Exploitation phase completely absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized BCU key writes, device lockout/purge commands from unauthenticated or out-of-band sources, and bulk configuration resets on KNX devices.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Inventory Gap / Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) flags exposed assets. Article calls for 'quick check across your fleet.' No asset-exposure baseline generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all KNX devices accessible from untrusted networks. Cross-reference with CVE-2023-4346 scanner results. Escalate any internet-exposed KNX installations for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Asset Exposure — Unauthenticated Accessibility
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states exploit applies to 'public-facing applications' and implies network exposure (T1190 context). Phrase: 'exploit public-facing application' in MITRE guidance; also 'federal civilian agencies required to remediate' implies active scans/exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX devices (port/service fingerprints) or KNX protocol traffic accessible from untrusted networks. Alert on inbound connections to KNX control services (typically TCP/3671 or UDP) from external subnets or internet-routable IPs.

suggestion.title: KNX Bulk Device Purge / Reset Events
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'purge all devices'. This is a system-wide manipulation action that would generate device deletion/wipe logs if captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk deletion or reset of KNX devices within a short time window. Look for API/management interface calls that delete multiple device objects, or firmware reset commands issued to multiple devices consecutively. Baseline: normal maintenance typically affects 1–3 devices; anomaly threshold >10 devices in 5 min.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Lock / Modification Events
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'set a BCU key to lock the device' as direct impact. BCU (Board Control Unit) key modification is a privileged action that should be audit-logged.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on attempts to read, modify, or lock BCU keys on KNX devices, especially when triggered by non-administrative or unexpected accounts. Flag any BCU key changes that do not correlate with scheduled maintenance or approved change requests.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Anomaly — Overly Restrictive Mechanism Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article vulnerability class: 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'. Attacker can exploit this to trigger mass lockouts. Phrase: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusually high rates of account lockout events on KNX control systems, especially if lockouts affect all or most accounts in a short window. Correlate with failed authentication attempts; if lockout rate is disproportionate to failed logins, suspect exploitation of the lockout vulnerability.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Device Purge Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' No detection hypothesis exists for bulk device removal or state-zeroing events in KNX environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network for sudden mass device state changes, bulk device removal commands, or configuration resets. Correlate with failed or bypassed authentication lockout events. KNX protocol analyzers should flag unauthorized purge commands on Option 1 deployments.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 BCU Key Lock Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific cryptographic/configuration manipulation. No detection for BCU (Building Controller Unit) key state changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected BCU key modifications, re-keying operations, or lock-state transitions. Monitor for commands that manipulate Building Controller Unit security parameters outside change-management windows.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets).' Standard exposure hunt template referenced but no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for KNX devices exposed on public/untrusted networks (ports 3671/UDP, 3672/TCP typical). Cross-reference inventory against CVE-2023-4346 product list. Correlate scanner findings with firewall logs for ingress attempts to KNX services.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Unauthorized Access via Lockout Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—suggests attacker can bypass or circumvent the lockout protection entirely. No detection for lockout-mechanism abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid authentication attempts following account lockout (should be blocked), successful authentications during lockout window, or lockout-mechanism disablement commands. Monitor for Option 1 deployments where lockout protections are absent or misconfigured.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'CVE-2023-4346' as the vulnerability identifier. Standard asset-exposure hunt template should fire for any vulnerability scanner detecting this CVE on KNX devices.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for vulnerability scan results or asset inventory updates identifying CVE-2023-4346 on KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 devices. Alert on any detection in federated vuln management systems.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge / Bulk Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' This implies programmatic bulk deletion capability; abnormal mass device removal should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device management APIs and logs for bulk device deletion or purge commands, especially those that affect 5+ devices in a short time window or without corresponding change tickets. Baseline normal device lifecycle events and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Modification Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'can set a BCU key to lock the device.' BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key changes should be rare and auditable; unauthorized modifications indicate compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modification of BCU cryptographic keys or authorization credentials on KNX devices, particularly bulk changes or changes originating from non-administrative IPs. Correlate with failed authentication attempts preceding key changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Authorization Option Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly an 'Account Lockout Mechanism' bypass. Exploit attempts would manifest as circumvention of normal authorization or brute-force patterns against KNX authentication endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for repeated failed authentication attempts against KNX devices that don't result in expected account lockout, or successful authentications immediately after excessive failed attempts. Track authorization option configuration changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Lockout Events
suggestion.rationale: Article notes attacker can 'lock the device' via BCU key manipulation. Simultaneous device locking or access denial across fleet segments suggests exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for correlated device unavailability or lock status events affecting multiple KNX devices in a short timeframe. Cross-reference with administrative actions; unexplained fleet-wide lockouts warrant immediate investigation.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Authentication Bypass / Device Purge
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—direct exploitation outcome requiring hunt coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol connections for unauthorized device purge commands or mass device state changes. Look for burst of device removal/reset events from single source or account within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific technical indicator of compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KNX Bus Coupling Unit (BCU) key changes from unauthorized sources or outside change-control windows. Flag any BCU key lock operations.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Exploit Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—suggests exploitation path via authorization bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt KNX protocol traffic for repeated failed authentication attempts followed by device state changes. Look for connection patterns that exploit the lockout mechanism bypass.

suggestion.title: Exposed KNX Protocol Interface Access from Internet
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates 'observed exploited in the wild'—KNX management interfaces must be inventory'd for exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed KNX protocol ports (typically UDP 3671). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2023-4346. Flag any external-to-internal connections to KNX devices.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV: Vulnerability Scan Match CVE-2023-4346

suggestion.title: Phishing form injection via XSS into install.php response
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'credential-phishing form injection' via form-action bypass. Article: 'The CSP is missing a form-action directive, allowing exploitation via credential-phishing form injection.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from admin/install.php containing injected <form> tags with action attributes pointing to external domains or unusual POST handlers. Look for responses where query-string parameters are reflected directly into <form action=...> attributes, especially with method=POST or targets to credential-harvesting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Meta-refresh / open-redirect injection in admin/install.php
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions explicit attack primitive: 'meta open redirects' enabled by missing form-action CSP directive. Article: 'allowing exploitation via credential-phishing form injection and <meta> open redirects.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect <meta> tags with http-equiv or refresh attributes in responses from /admin/install.php, especially when the content attribute points to external domain (indicator of redirect injection). Match against query parameters reflected into meta tags.

suggestion.title: CSP form-action directive absence detection on admin install script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies the root cause: 'CSP is missing a form-action directive'. Detection of this misconfiguration enables proactive remediation. Article: 'A Content Security Policy (script-src 'self') prevents inline JavaScript execution, but the CSP is missing a form-action directive...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response headers for Content-Security-Policy on /admin/install.php. Alert when CSP is present but missing form-action directive or form-action is set to 'self'/'none'. Absence of CSP entirely on install script is highest-risk indicator.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated probe for install.php on production endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes installation script should never be accessible post-deployment: 'install.php should be removed or restricted'. Repeated successful HTTP 200 access by unauthenticated user indicates either misconfiguration or reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated HTTP GET requests to /admin/install.php, /install.php, or similar installer endpoints with HTTP 200 response. Prioritize when requests originate from external IP or show progressive payload testing (repeated requests with different query parameters).

suggestion.title: XSS payload reflection in print_test_result() output
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies the vulnerable function by name: 'User-supplied parameters are echoed into HTML without escaping via print_test_result()'. Direct detection of this function's output catching attacker-controlled input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses from install.php containing unescaped reflections of query parameters, particularly those matching known XSS payload patterns: script tags, event handlers (onerror, onload), HTML meta tags, or form-action injections. WAF signatures should match patterns seen in UC_8_5 (form, meta, http-equiv, onerror, onload).

suggestion.title: MantisBT self-registration followed by SOAP API replay from same source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'self-registration is enabled' on default installs and recommends hunt UC_10_2 for 'self-registration followed by SOAP API replay from same source IP.' Pipeline failed to extract this existing recommended hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on source IPs that hit signup.php followed by mantisconnect.php (SOAP endpoint) within a short window, indicating account creation then immediate API exploitation. Look for rapid signup-to-SOAP patterns suggesting automation.

suggestion.title: High-volume SOAP endpoint POST requests (mass enumeration/exfiltration)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends UC_10_3 for 'SOAP endpoint high-volume request burst' detecting mass data exfiltration, explicitly noting this as a phase:actions indicator for CVE-2026-47156 at Medium confidence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal SOAP query volume per source IP. Flag sources making >100 POST requests to mantisconnect.php in 10-minute windows, with particular attention to large response bytes. Timing correlation with SOAP auth events strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: Privilege escalation: SOAP-authenticated access to admin account functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'can authenticate as any other user (knowing their username), including the administrator' — this is privilege escalation but no detection covers the post-auth admin activity. Missing lateral movement detection after the bypass succeeds.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After successful SOAP auth via reused cookie, monitor for operations performed under admin context (user_id=1 or admin flag in SOAP logs). Correlate SOAP login_string reuse events with downstream admin-level operations (config changes, user deletion, role modification). Flag if admin functions called from non-administrative source IPs.

suggestion.title: SOAP API session cookie exfiltration (cookie value reuse across distinct sources)
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'Any user knowing any valid cookie_string can authenticate as any other user.' No detection suggested for the session-cookie exfiltration or cross-source reuse pattern. Article mentions T1539 (Steal Web Session Cookie) but no hunt covers detecting that cookie in use from unexpected source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all SOAP login_string values (or hash them). Detect when same session cookie is used from multiple distinct source IPs within a time window, or same cookie reappears hours/days later from different geography — indicates exfiltration and reuse.

suggestion.title: GitHub Release Tag Redirection to Orphaned Commit
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The attacker deleted the original version tags and relocated them to the malicious commit, which was the orphaned commit.' This is defense evasion: using legitimate-looking version identifiers (v35) to obscure malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect git tag creation or movement that points to commits orphaned from all branches, or tag reassignments that differ from commit lineage expectations. Monitor for version tags (v\d+) suddenly referencing orphaned commits in public-facing repositories with high downstream dependency counts.

suggestion.title: Orphaned Commit Creation in Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Having the attack commit orphaned from any branches, including the main branch' as a key enabling factor. Orphaned commits are abnormal and warrant alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when commits are created but never merged to any branch (remain unreachable from main/release branches). Cross-reference with tag creation to detect orphaned commits immediately claimed by release tags. High signal in repositories with CI/CD dependency.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Secrets Leaked to Plaintext in CI/CD Logs
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext in the GitHub Action logs.' Article describes deliberate secret exposure in public logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan GitHub Actions logs for patterns matching AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, private keys, or other secret prefixes in plaintext. Correlate with workflow changes that modified secret handling or debug/echo statements. Flag any secrets appearing in public logs (world-readable repos).

suggestion.title: Anomalous External Network Calls from GitHub Actions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The attack relied on making an external network call to pull down the attack code, which ultimately led to it being noticed by services that monitor anomalous network activity.' This was the detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound network connections from GitHub Actions runners to non-standard ports or suspicious domains. Baseline expected dependencies (package repos, S3, etc.) and alert on deviations. Flag runners fetching code from untrusted sources or using obfuscated domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Commit to High-Dependency Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'a malicious actor had write access to a repo that 23,000 other repos relied on.' Any commit to such repos should undergo scrutiny for code changes affecting CI/CD or secret handling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For repositories with >1000 dependent repos (detected via GitHub API), alert on commits that modify secret-handling code, GitHub Actions workflow files, or add network calls. Require high-confidence authorship verification and correlate with push access provisioning.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modification Affecting Secret Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes code that 'caused encrypted secrets to appear in plaintext.' This requires modifying how secrets are handled in workflow YAML or action code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect changes to GitHub Actions workflows or action code that remove secret masking, add echo/debug statements outputting secret environment variables, or disable log obfuscation. Flag commits adding `::set-output` or `::debug` statements that reference secret contexts.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an attacker to purge all devices without additional security options enabled'—explicit impact capability requiring detection. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network for bulk reset/purge commands to multiple devices within short timeframe. Baseline normal purge operations and alert on anomalous patterns. Cross-reference target device IPs against asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized BCU Key Lock Operation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attacker capability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—specific post-exploitation impact activity. Pipeline generated zero use cases for device lock patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on BCU key modification events from unexpected sources or at irregular times. Monitor for mass BCU lock operations. Track authorization failures preceding successful locks.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerable Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries are in-the-wild exploited vulnerabilities requiring immediate asset hunting. Article identifies vulnerable product with federal remediation deadline 2026-07-29. Pipeline returned empty IOC set—failed to extract CVE as primary search indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2023-4346. Cross-reference asset inventory for 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' devices. Flag instances on external-facing segments or lacking compensating controls.

suggestion.title: KNX Authentication Bypass via Lockout Mechanism Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—the lockout logic itself is weaponized. Devices without 'additional security options' are vulnerable. Article implies credential/access-control attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX devices for rapid failed authentication attempts followed by unexpected privilege gain or device control. Flag lockout logic anomalies. Alert on authorization state changes post-lockout.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Inventory — CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'purge all devices' — detection starts with knowing what KNX assets exist. Article mentions 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' and 'BCU key' which are KNX-specific identifiers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify KNX devices on the network via EDS (Electronic Device Specification) announcements, UDP port 3671, or IEC 101/104 protocol signatures. Baseline known-good KNX devices; flag new or unexpected KNX participants.

suggestion.title: KNX Exploitation Attempt — CVE-2023-4346 Protocol Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'Connection Authorization Option 1' — this is a protocol-level vulnerability. Need to detect malformed or unauthorized KNX protocol messages attempting to bypass authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network traffic for connection attempts lacking proper BCU key challenge-response, unauthorized telegramming, or bypass of the overly-restrictive lockout mechanism. Look for rapid connection attempts or invalid authorization sequences.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Lockout/Purge Detection — CVE-2023-4346 Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'purge all devices' and 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' These are high-confidence impact indicators that warrant detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNX telegram messages that clear device memory (purge commands), modify BCU keys, or trigger lockout states. Look for batch device resets, loss of device responsiveness in groups, or emergency shutdown commands in KNX logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Vulnerability Scan Results — KNX Asset Remediation
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV sets federal patch due-date of 2026-07-29. Need tracking of scan results showing vulnerable KNX devices to measure remediation progress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Consume vulnerability scan results (Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7, etc.) filtered for CVE-2023-4346. Identify KNX devices with 'vulnerable' status, group by risk tier, and alert on devices still unpatched as patch-due-date approaches (2026-07-29).

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Reconnaissance — Pre-Exploitation Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes device-level attacks but does not mention reconnaissance. However, KNX attackers must discover topology and device types before exploitation; missing detection for network scanning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for KNX broadcast storms, group address scanning, or repeated parameter read requests (GroupValueRead telegrams) against unknown or all group addresses. Baseline normal KNX traffic patterns and alert on anomalies suggesting topology enumeration.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Lockout or Purge Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device.' No detection rule was generated for this core attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for KNX protocol frames indicating device state changes (offline, reset, lockout). Alert on bulk device lockout events or rapid sequence of device purge commands. Correlate with successful authentication to KNX management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Connection Authorization Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Connection Authorization Option 1' as the vulnerable feature, yet pipeline suggests no detection for unauthorized modifications to this access control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for changes to KNX Connection Authorization settings, particularly Option 1 feature toggles or account lockout policy modifications. Flag any disabling or override of security-relevant authorization mechanisms.

suggestion.title: KNX Management Interface Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation must transit a KNX management interface or bus access point; article does not specify path but implies remote or local access to trigger lockout/purge. Pipeline failed to generate access-control detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed authentication attempts against KNX management interfaces followed by successful login. Detect connections from unexpected source IPs or outside-hours access. Correlate with subsequent device state changes.

suggestion.title: Bulk KNX Device State Synchronization Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'purge all devices' suggests coordinated multi-device impact. Pipeline generated no detection for abnormal bulk-device state transitions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal patterns in KNX device status changes—rapid simultaneous offline events, synchronized configuration resets, or coordinated firmware/state rollback across multiple devices in the same KNX area.

suggestion.title: HTTP/3 Server Crash via Malformed QUIC Ring Buffer Overflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Unpatched XRING Flaw...Lets Remote Clients Crash HTTP/3 Servers'—direct availability impact from remote unauthenticated request. Pipeline generated zero detection logic for this primary threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected termination of QUIC/HTTP/3 server processes (h3-server, xquic, quiche) with preceding UDP 443 packet anomalies: out-of-order frame offsets, oversized stream-offset fields, or malformed QUIC variable-length integers indicating ring-buffer trigger.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: QUIC/HTTP/3 Server Implementation Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must identify vulnerable XQUIC instances. Detection gap: no rules for Version Negotiation probes, Alt-Svc header enumeration, or TLS certificate fingerprinting targeting HTTP/3 services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repeated QUIC Version Negotiation (0x6b3343cf) requests to port 443 from single IP, or connection attempts with invalid version bytes followed by rapid reconnection—consistent with capability probing.

suggestion.title: Malformed QUIC Frame Delivery and Server Availability Loss
suggestion.rationale: XRING is a ring-buffer overflow triggered by specific QUIC frame sequences. Article describes remote crash without detailing payload, but detection should flag abnormal offset/length combinations in STREAM, CRYPTO, or data frames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect UDP 443 traffic with QUIC packets containing stream offsets exceeding connection-level max_stream_data_bidi_local, duplicate offset values within single connection, or offset increments inconsistent with previous frames—followed by host-level process crash or port unavailability.

suggestion.title: KNX CVE-2023-4346 Exploitation Attempts (T1190)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'T1190 — Exploit Public-Facing Application (KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets)' as the primary attack vector. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite known-exploited status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on anomalous KNX protocol connection attempts, unauthorized handshakes to KNX gateways/controllers, or protocol manipulation attempts from untrusted networks targeting the vulnerable 'Connection Authorization Option 1' component.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge and BCU Key Lockout
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device'—explicit device-destruction impact that requires dedicated detection. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk device deletion commands, factory-reset operations, or BCU key modification/lockout events in KNX system logs. Correlate with prior T1190 exploitation activity; alert on sequences suggesting coordinated device sabotage.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance Hunt
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries canonically require asset-inventory hunts; federal patch due-date is 2026-07-29. Article template explicitly references 'asset-exposure' hunt pattern, yet pipeline generated zero UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for KNX Association products with 'Connection Authorization Option 1' component active. Prioritize devices with network exposure (WAN, untrusted VLANs); flag unpatched instances and generate remediation tickets against the 2026-07-29 deadline.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Mechanism Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability description emphasizes 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' as the exploit vector. Pipeline should detect abuse of this mechanism as authentication/access-denial attack, but generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX system logs for bulk account lockout events, authentication failures preceding device state changes, or rapid lock/unlock cycles suggesting lockout-mechanism exploitation. Baseline against normal maintenance patterns.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 KNX Device Inventory & Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2023-4346 affecting KNX Protocol systems with federal remediation due 2026-07-29. No IOCs or asset-exposure UC were generated despite this being a CISA KEV entry requiring immediate inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB and vulnerability scanners for 'KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' products. Cross-reference against CVE-2023-4346 scoring. Identify internet-facing or untrusted-network-adjacent KNX devices. Establish baseline of known-compliant versions by vendor patch date.

suggestion.title: KNX Unauthorized Device Purge Events
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker capability to 'purge all devices without additional security options'—direct impact indicator. No impact-phase UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX system logs for bulk device removal/reset commands. Correlate with failed BCU authorization attempts or anomalous access patterns. Alert when device count decreases unexpectedly or when purge commands originate from non-administrative accounts/IPs.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Lock Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—indicates attacker persistence & denial of service. No UC targets this post-exploitation hardening.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline BCU key modification events (rotation schedule, authorized admins). Alert on unexpected key changes, especially those followed by device lockout or inaccessibility. Correlate key modifications with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: KNX Authorization Mechanism Abuse Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—attackers abuse this control itself. No UC targets the lockout-bypass attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track repeated authentication failures on KNX devices followed by successful access without re-authentication delay (indicating lockout mechanism bypass). Flag accounts/IPs that trigger lockout thresholds repeatedly then succeed.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Service Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'KNX Association KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1' devices as exploitable. The pipeline's own template section instructed: 'Standard asset-exposure hunt...Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>: CVE: CVE-2023-4346'. This was not executed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for KNXnet/IP services (typically UDP/3671) across managed network. Cross-reference with CVE-2023-4346 presence from vulnerability scanner. Alert on unauthorized connection attempts to KNX devices, especially from external or untrusted subnets.

suggestion.title: Device Purge Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could...purge all devices without additional security options enabled'. This is a concrete post-exploitation behavioral indicator requiring detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk device reset, factory-reset, or purge operations targeting KNX devices. Correlate with administrative account access to KNX management consoles. Alert on high-volume device state-change events in compressed timeframes (e.g., 50+ devices modified within 60 seconds).

suggestion.title: BCU Key Lock Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device', indicating a persistence or denial-of-service post-exploitation action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) configuration changes, especially key field modifications. Alert on unexpected key-locking operations against production KNX devices. Cross-check administrative access logs for unauthorized configuration changes.

suggestion.title: KNX Service Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article presupposes network-accessible KNX devices ('purge all devices without additional security options enabled'). CISA KEV mandates asset-exposure assessment; none was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal and internet-facing networks for exposed KNX services (EIB/KNX typically port 3671/UDP). Identify instances running KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 and cross-reference against patch status for CVE-2023-4346. Prioritize remediation per federal due date 2026-07-29.

suggestion.title: Bulk KNX Device Purge Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' No detection hypothesis for anomalous mass device deletion was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX network management systems for rapid, sequential device deletions or bulk purge operations. Baseline normal device lifecycle patterns and alert on anomalies, especially those originating from untrusted network segments or unauthenticated sessions.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Lockout Configuration Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' No detection for unauthorized BCU key manipulation or unexpected device lockout was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Building Control Unit (BCU) key configuration events for unauthorized key sets or modifications. Alert on any BCU key manipulation from non-administrative sources or outside scheduled maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: KNX Auth-Lockout Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability characterized as 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism.' Article states attacker can exploit this 'without additional security options enabled'—implies auth controls are bypassable. No detection for auth-bypass attempts generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect repeated KNX authentication failures followed by successful lockout bypass, key reset, or direct device access. Baseline normal lockout/recovery patterns and alert on anomalies indicative of authentication mechanism exploitation.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Exploit Attempt Detection — CVE-2023-4346
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes exploitation of KNX protocol authorization bypass allowing device purge and BCU key lock. T1190 is mapped. No use case was generated despite template reference at `_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected KNX protocol traffic (ports 3671 UDP, 12671 TCP) from non-whitelisted sources targeting organization's building-automation or industrial-control gateways. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner for unpatched KNX devices with CVE-2023-4346.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Mass Purge or Unauthorized Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'purge all devices' and 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—these are post-exploitation impact operations indicating successful compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk device removal, reset, or configuration-lock commands via KNX management interface or protocol traffic. Flag any Bus Coupling Unit (BCU) key modifications outside scheduled maintenance. Baseline normal device lifecycle and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Mechanism Flooding
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' as the exploitation vector. Attacker abuse of this lockout would be a telltale pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential failed-authentication attempts against KNX device administrative accounts or BCU access interfaces. Flag lockout events that occur outside change-control windows or from atypical source IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2023-4346 Exposure Scan Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' substituting CVE-2023-4346; pipeline generated zero hunts despite this direct instruction and KEV status (actively exploited).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detections of CVE-2023-4346 across KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 instances. Prioritize externally-facing or Internet-accessible assets; KEV status indicates active wild exploitation.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article defines vulnerability as 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' allowing bypass 'without additional security options enabled'. No detection mapped for auth bypass or lockout circumvention attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed KNX authentication events followed by successful access without re-authentication, or rapid auth failure/success cycles suggesting lockout reset exploitation. Correlate with subsequent admin actions.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Mass Device Purge
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could allow an attacker to purge all devices'. No detection suggested for purge operations or bulk device removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KNX device purge commands affecting multiple devices, especially without standard security option validation. Escalate if preconditions show auth anomalies or lockout events.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Modification to Locked State
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker capability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device'. This persistence/DoS indicator was not mapped to any detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key state changes, especially transitions to locked state. Flag unauthorized key modifications from non-admin accounts or atypical modification timings.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Enumeration and Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers target 'public-facing' KNX endpoints; enumeration precedes exploitation. No UC generated to detect port scans or connection probes against KNX protocol ports (typically 3671/TCP) or connection attempts from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated connection attempts to KNX protocol ports from external or unauthenticated sources. Alert on TCP 3671 traffic from non-whitelisted IPs or sustained scanning patterns indicative of asset discovery.

suggestion.title: BCU Key Modification and Authorization Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states threat is ability to 'set a BCU key to lock the device' — a direct manipulation of device authorization. No UC to detect unauthorized writes to BCU configuration or key material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any write operations to BCU key fields or authorization tables within KNX endpoint logs. Alert on key updates from non-administrative sources or out-of-change-control windows.

suggestion.title: Mass Device Purge or State Reset
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'purge all devices without additional security options enabled.' Pipeline missed the most damaging phase — bulk device removal is both unusual and high-confidence malicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX controller event logs for rapid, synchronized device deletion or state-reset commands. Alert if >5 devices are purged within a 10-minute window from a single session or source.

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Pattern Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' — attacker weaponizes this to lock legitimate accounts. No UC to detect abnormal lockout rates or lockout-then-action sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid failed authentication attempts against KNX admin accounts with subsequent device purge or BCU key modification events. Alert on >3 lockouts in 5 minutes followed by state changes, indicating exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized KNX Connection Authorization Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is in 'Connection Authorization Option 1' — attackers bypass authentication. No UC to detect connections that succeed despite authorization policies or that use non-standard/malformed auth sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX connection logs for authentication method deviations (e.g., connections using Option 1 when Option 1 should be disabled). Alert on successful connections from sources that previously failed authorization.

suggestion.title: Protocol Anomaly — Invalid or Malformed KNX Commands
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of 'overly restrictive' mechanism implies attacker sends crafted commands that trigger unexpected behavior. No UC to detect malformed KNX protocol sequences or commands that violate schema.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag KNX control messages that violate protocol specification (invalid APDU structure, out-of-sequence commands, or reserved fields in use). Baseline expected command distribution and alert on >10% anomalous messages per session.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Exploitation Attempt — Device Purge
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow an attacker to purge all devices'—explicit impact description that warrants detection of unexpected device deletion or mass device purge commands within KNX deployments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol traffic and device logs for purge/reset commands issued without corresponding administrative action. Alert on unexpected removal of multiple devices from KNX configuration within short time window, especially if preceded by unauthorized protocol access.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'set a BCU key to lock the device'—direct evidence of attacker capability to modify device-level cryptographic keys, warranting detection of BCU key write operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect modification of BCU (Basic Control Unit) keys on KNX devices. Monitor for key-setting commands in KNX protocol traffic and device firmware logs; flag any BCU key changes that do not correlate with scheduled maintenance or authenticated administrator sessions.

suggestion.title: KNX Asset Exposure — Unauthenticated Protocol Access
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry confirms active exploitation in wild; article describes vulnerability in 'Connection Authorization Option 1'—justifies hunt for exposed KNX devices accepting unauthenticated or weakly-authenticated protocol connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed KNX protocol listeners (typically UDP 3671, TCP 3672 for KNX/IP interface). Detect failed and successful unauthenticated connection attempts to KNX devices. Correlate exposed device inventory against patched versions to identify remediation gaps.

suggestion.title: KNX Authorization Bypass — Failed Lockout Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability is 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism'—attackers bypass authentication via lockout exhaustion. Detection should capture repeated failed authentication attempts that should trigger lockout but do not.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX device authentication logs for repeated failed connection attempts that exceed defined lockout thresholds without triggering account lock. Alert on authentication attempt patterns consistent with lockout mechanism bypass exploitation.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Enrollment/Disenrollment Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Exploit allows 'purge all devices'; detection should include baseline of normal device lifecycle changes and flag mass or unauthorized device configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of normal KNX device addition/removal rates. Alert on sudden spikes in device removal events, unauthorized device disenrollment, or deletion of critical infrastructure devices from KNX topology without corresponding change tickets.

suggestion.title: KNX System Reconnaissance — Topology and Device Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Before exploitation, attackers must enumerate KNX devices and topology; article confirms active exploitation, implying reconnaissance precedes attacks. Detect scanning or enumeration of KNX address space and device properties.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for systematic scanning of KNX address groups or device addresses. Detect enumeration of KNX device properties (e.g., group address listings, device descriptors) by unauthorized sources. Flag sequential or sweep-pattern access to KNX protocol endpoints.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt: CVE-2023-4346 Public-Facing KNX Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends asset-exposure hunt via template substitution; this is the canonical first detection for any CISA KEV entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query your asset-management and vulnerability-scanning systems for instances of KNX Protocol Connection Authorization Option 1 running on internet-facing assets. Cross-reference against patch status and federal remediation deadline (2026-07-29). This is passive inventory-based detection, not behavioral.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Device Lockout / Device Purge
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could allow...purge all devices without additional security options enabled and set a BCU key to lock the device.' This is explicit impact activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected account lockout events or device purge commands originating from unauthorized sources or abnormal IP ranges. Monitor BCU (Bus Coupling Unit) key modification events for unauthorized changes. Baseline normal lockout rates and alert on sudden spikes.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ability to 'set a BCU key' without authorization, implying configuration changes. Monitor for unauthorized writes to device configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modifications to KNX device configuration, specifically BCU key changes, lockout policy alterations, or security option disabling. Focus on changes originating from non-admin accounts or out-of-band channels.

suggestion.title: KNX Protocol Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application); need network-level detection of exploitation attempts against KNX services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor KNX protocol endpoints for exploitation patterns: malformed authentication sequences, repeated authorization failures on public-facing ports, or protocol violations consistent with CVE-2023-4346 exploitation (e.g., account lockout abuse, overly permissive lockout bypass attempts).

suggestion.title: Account Lockout Mechanism Abuse on KNX Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism' as the vulnerability vector. Attackers leverage this to trigger device lockout or purge functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid, repeated authentication failures against KNX systems followed by account lockout events, particularly if combined with subsequent device purge or BCU key-setting commands. Baseline normal failure rates per user/device.

suggestion.title: KNX Device Purge or Mass Removal Event Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'could purge all devices' as primary impact. No use case captures device removal, purge, or bulk state-change events from KNX infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on KNX device purge, removal, or deletion events, especially bulk operations affecting multiple devices within a short time window. Correlate with failed or anomalous authentication attempts on the KNX gateway or controller that precede the purge.

suggestion.title: KNX BCU Key Manipulation or Locking Events
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker can 'set a BCU key to lock the device.' This is a specific persistence and impact mechanism that generic exploitation hunts do not cover.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BCU (Basic Control Unit) key creation, modification, or setting events on KNX devices. Flag any unauthorized BCU key changes outside documented maintenance windows or change-control records.

suggestion.title: KNX Account Lockout Anomaly Detection – Exploitation Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly exploits 'overly restrictive account lockout mechanism.' Detection must hunt lockout events that trigger the exploit path, not generic failed authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid or sustained account lockout events on KNX devices or gateways. Correlate lockout event spikes with subsequent device purge or BCU key manipulation events. Establish per-device baseline lockout rates.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated or Anomalous KNX Gateway Access – Public-Facing Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is cited in the article. Detection should hunt successful or attempted access to exposed KNX gateways from external networks post-authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP(S) or KNX protocol connections to KNX gateways or controllers from non-internal IP ranges. Correlate with user-agent strings or protocol anomalies consistent with exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: KNX Connection Authorization Option 1 Protocol Bypass Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability resides in 'Connection Authorization Option 1' mechanism. Detection should surface protocol-level authorization bypass or manipulation, not just post-exploitation device events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect KNX protocol frames for malformed or missing authorization fields in the Connection Authorization Option 1 handshake. Flag any deviations from specification compliance.

suggestion.title: WordPress Backdoor / Webshell File Upload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'WP-SHELLSTORM Backdooring Thousands of WordPress Sites'—implies file upload or shell installation into WordPress directories. Pipeline missed execution vector and persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor WordPress plugin/theme upload directories for unexpected .php files, particularly those with obfuscated names or timestamped just after known exploitation attempts. Alert on wp-content/uploads or similar paths receiving .php writes outside normal deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution from Web-Writable Directory
suggestion.rationale: Backdoors deployed to WordPress sites must execute PHP code. Article references 'backdooring'—implies post-execution command and control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php-cgi, php.exe) launched from wp-content/uploads, wp-includes, or other writable paths. Correlate with unusual command-line arguments, parent process mismatches (e.g., not Apache/nginx), or system commands executed during PHP process lifetime.
