suggestion.title: Post-RCE Lateral Movement from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article does not rule out attacker pivot post-exploitation. Pipeline should detect credential theft, network recon, or lateral movement originating from compromised FortiSandbox context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for discovery commands (whoami, systeminfo, net user) or credential-access (SAM reads, LSASS access) from FortiSandbox process trees. Detect SMB/RDP lateral connections initiated from appliance.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Inventory & Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS' with federal patch due 2026-07-19. Asset exposure hunting is the canonical first step for any KEV entry. Standard template applies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiSandbox instances (on-prem, cloud, PaaS) via network scanning, asset inventory, and cloud API queries. Match against CVE-2026-25089 in scanner data. Flag instances where reported patch level contradicts vulnerability scan results or last update date is older than patch release.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector in article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'. This is the exploitation primitive requiring network and application-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (443, 8080) for payloads containing command injection signatures: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe operators, or URL-encoded shell metacharacters in query parameters or POST bodies. Unauthenticated requests (missing/invalid auth headers) from external IPs are high-signal. Spike detection on malformed requests is secondary.

suggestion.title: Anomalous OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Successful HTTP-based command injection results in unauthorized OS-level command execution. Article: 'execute unauthorized commands'. Process monitoring is the evidence layer for successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox system processes (typically root, fortisandbox user, or system service account). Baseline normal FortiSandbox process trees. Flag any bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell, or interpreter invocations outside known maintenance windows. Cross-correlate with external HTTP requests in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Explicit CVE identifier in CISA KEV entry must be matched against all FortiSandbox instances. Article: 'CVE-2026-25089'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run Nessus/Qualys/Rapid7 or equivalent against all FortiSandbox assets targeting CVE-2026-25089. Alert on any positive match. Create incident for each confirmed vulnerable instance with remediation deadline 2026-07-19. Correlate scanner findings with patch management system to identify patch installation failures.

suggestion.title: External API/Endpoint Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker' as threat actor. Cloud and PaaS deployments are externally facing and more likely to be directly probed. Requires API-level logging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS API access logs for requests with missing, invalid, or expired authentication tokens. Alert on spike in HTTP 401/403 responses from external IPs. Ratio of auth failures to successes or requests from never-before-seen geolocations are secondary indicators of scanning/reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Exploit Public-Facing Application - WordPress Core RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'Unauthenticated RCE in WordPress core'—the attack vector is unauthenticated exploitation of a web application. This is T1190 classic, and pipeline should have surfaced detection for HTTP requests attempting to trigger the flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to WordPress core endpoints with suspicious parameter combinations, unusual user-agent strings, or payloads indicative of code injection. Look for requests to unpatched WordPress versions from unauthenticated sources. Correlate with subsequent execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Command Execution via PHP - Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE in WordPress implies arbitrary code execution, typically PHP on Linux hosts. Pipeline must detect post-exploit activity: process spawning, reverse shells, or command-line invocations from web worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous child processes spawned by web server daemons (apache, nginx, php-fpm) with suspicious command lines (nc, bash, curl, wget, or interpreted languages). Flag executions of scripting interpreters from /var/www or equivalent web root directories.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence - PHP File Writes
suggestion.rationale: RCE often results in web shell implantation for persistence. Article does not detail post-exploitation behavior, but critical RCEs typically include persistence indicators: anomalous file writes to web-accessible directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation of .php, .phtml, or .php5 files in WordPress directories (wp-content, wp-admin, themes, plugins) outside of known deploy/update windows. Correlate timing with prior HTTP exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Database Access from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: WordPress RCE enables database exfiltration or manipulation. Attackers typically execute MySQL/MariaDB queries for data theft or backdoor account insertion. Pipeline should alert on abnormal query patterns from web processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect direct TCP connections from web daemons to database ports (3306) with suspicious query patterns: CREATE USER, GRANT, SELECT INTO, or LOAD_FILE operations. Flag multi-megabyte data transfers from database to web process in short windows.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 from Compromised WordPress
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attacker typically establishes command-and-control. Unauthenticated RCE often leads to botnet enrollment or reverse shell establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from web server processes to non-canonical destinations (non-CDN, non-WordPress.com, non-trusted update servers). Flag connections to known C2 IP ranges or domains with suspicious TLS certificates.

suggestion.title: Patch Status Assessment - WordPress Core Versions
suggestion.rationale: Title includes 'wp2shell' context suggesting specific version or component. Detection must include inventory of unpatched WordPress installations to enable rapid response. Pipeline failed to extract version indicators or patch-level requirements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query WordPress installations for core version in HTTP headers, readme.html, or js/css versioning. Cross-reference against CVE database for wp2shell to identify vulnerable instances. Alert when unpatched versions are exposed to internet.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation — Vite Ecosystem
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'seven malicious Vite npm packages' but zero packages extracted. Detection must identify compromised package installations with malicious post-install scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install targeting Vite-related packages. Alert on packages with obfuscated postinstall hooks, excessive hidden dependencies, or registration within 30 days. Cross-reference against npm audit advisory feeds and supply-chain threat databases.

suggestion.title: Blockchain C2 Network Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Blockchain C2' but zero command-and-control detection generated. Must identify blockchain-based covert channels (RPC endpoints, blockchain explorers, wallet services).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS/HTTP queries to blockchain infrastructure: etherscan.io, infura.io, alchemy.com, blockchain.com, or direct Ethereum/Bitcoin RPC endpoints. Detect repeated wallet address lookups from same process. Flag cryptocurrency service domains accessed from development/build contexts.

suggestion.title: Child Process Execution from npm/Node During Package Install
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages execute code at install-time via postinstall hooks, but pipeline missed execution-layer detection. Article implies RAT installed via build-time scripts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for node.js spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash during npm install/build phases. Detect obfuscated or base64-encoded script payloads. Alert on file writes to non-project directories and unexpected network connections initiated from build processes.

suggestion.title: RAT Persistence Mechanism Installation by Build Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states packages 'deliver a RAT' but zero persistence detection generated. Expected: registry modifications, Startup folder writes, or scheduled task creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Run key modifications, AppData persistence, Startup folder writes, scheduled task creation, or service installation triggered by npm/node processes. Alert on any persistence tactic established outside legitimate project build.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated npm Package Script Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Malicious postinstall hooks employ obfuscation (base64, Unicode escapes, eval); article indicates sophisticated attack, yet pipeline missed script-level analysis of package.json payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract npm package.json postinstall/preinstall scripts. Decode base64 and escaped strings. Alert on eval(), exec(), or Function() constructors. Compare against malicious package signatures and deobfuscation heuristics.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Interaction and Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: RAT targeting development/crypto users likely exfiltrates to blockchain wallets or DeFi protocols; zero exfiltration detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected blockchain wallet creation, fund transfers, or smart-contract interactions from development machines. Monitor for cryptographic operations in JavaScript (webcrypto, signing APIs). Alert on transfer of credentials or secrets to blockchain addresses.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Token Harvesting or Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states NadMesh 'hunts...Kubernetes tokens.' Detection must cover reads of kubeconfig files, ServiceAccount token access, and in-cluster credential enumeration by bot processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process reads of ~/.kube/config, /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token, or environment variable KUBECONFIG access by suspicious/bot processes. Flag Kubernetes API calls (GET /api/v1/namespaces/{}/secrets) from non-standard principals or external IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Material Discovery and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hunts exposed AI services for cloud keys'—direct credential theft objective. Detection scope: AWS access keys, GCP credentials, Azure keys in environment, config files, container registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect subprocess reads/cat of .aws/credentials, .kube/config, .gcp directories. Flag process execution of aws ec2 describe, gcloud auth list, az account show by non-admin/bot user context. Monitor env variable reads for AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, KUBECONFIG.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Exposed AI Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: NadMesh 'hunts exposed AI services'—implies active service discovery and probing phase preceding credential theft. Detection must cover port scanning, endpoint enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential connection attempts to common AI service API ports (8000–8888, 5000, typical model-serving ranges). Flag scanning patterns targeting OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, or local LLM endpoints. Alert on HTTP/HTTPS probing of /.well-known/, /v1/models, /api/status paths.

suggestion.title: NadMesh Botnet Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names malware family 'NadMesh.' Pipeline must emit detection for binary execution, module loading, and C2 beaconing tied to this specific threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation matching NadMesh signatures (file hashes, command lines, parent-child chains if signatures are available). Monitor for network connections from known NadMesh C2 domains or IPs. Alert on DLL injection, process hollowing, or memory-write patterns indicative of botnet execution.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Kubernetes Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Stolen K8s tokens enable cluster-wide lateral movement. Detection must cover suspicious pod/service account creation, privilege escalation, and cross-namespace token usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new service accounts with cluster-admin or elevated RBAC bindings post-compromise. Detect pods deployed in unusual namespaces using stolen service account tokens. Flag API calls to create/modify ClusterRoles, ClusterRoleBindings, or Secrets from unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Stolen Cloud API Keys
suggestion.rationale: Harvested cloud keys enable persistent infrastructure access. Detection must cover unauthorized IAM/access-key activity, cross-account role assumption, and long-term credential establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls (CreateAccessKey, CreateUser, AssumeRole) using compromised credentials. Flag unusual principal/IP combinations using stolen keys for resource enumeration or instance/database access. Alert on federated identity setup or cross-account role assumption by non-service principals.

suggestion.title: Execution of processes signed with DigiCert certificates matching breach indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article describes GoldenEyeDog theft of DigiCert code-signing certificates for malware distribution; should detect process execution signed with DigiCert certs issued during/after breach or matching leaked thumbprints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ProcessSignatureStatus and Signer fields for processes with DigiCert Authenticode signatures. Flag execution of binaries with certificate thumbprints known to be compromised in breach, or DigiCert-signed software from publishers not historically signed by DigiCert. Cross-validate against software asset inventory.

suggestion.title: Code-signed malware delivery from GoldenEyeDog infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes weaponization: stolen DigiCert certs used to sign malware for distribution. Requires detection of signed executables from known GoldenEyeDog C2 or drop sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag downloaded/executed files bearing Authenticode signature with DigiCert and source IP/domain in threat-intel feeds for GoldenEyeDog C2 or known malware distribution servers. Signature presence should NOT suppress alert when source is malicious; code-signing trust must be revoked for compromised certificates.

suggestion.title: Abnormal certificate issuer transitions in process execution lineage
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise indicates software signed by one CA (vendor) may now bear different signer (DigiCert leak). Detection should catch CA substitution in signing chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline signing certificate issuer per software package. Alert when process execution shows issuer mismatch (e.g., vendor software previously signed by vendor CA now signed by DigiCert). Especially high-confidence if new issuer is DigiCert but vendor is not in known DigiCert-signed software list.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance targeting software vendor build/signing infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of DigiCert implies prior reconnaissance within partner environments or build infrastructure. Should detect enumeration/scanning of certificate stores, code repositories, or signing systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-system enumeration (dir, ls, find) or registry queries (Get-ChildItem on CERT stores) targeting directories containing certificates, code artifacts, or signing materials on systems in supplier/vendor networks. Correlate with network reconnaissance (DNS to vendor domains, port scans to build-system IP ranges).

suggestion.title: Lateral movement to code-signing or certificate management infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must reach certificate vaults or signing systems to exfiltrate DigiCert certs. Should detect RDP/SSH/SMB to code-signing systems or unusual process execution on signing servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inbound RDP/SSH/SMB connections to systems in signing/certificate infrastructure from external or unusual internal hosts. Alert on process execution (certutil.exe, powershell.exe, openssl) on signing infrastructure with command-line indicating certificate export, import, or listing.

suggestion.title: Certificate revocation list (CRL) or OCSP bypass/suppression
suggestion.rationale: GoldenEyeDog must ensure stolen certificates evade revocation checks. Detection should catch suppression of CRL/OCSP validation or cache poisoning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications disabling certificate revocation checks (e.g., SetReg CertCheckMode, DisableCRLChecks). Alert on WinHTTP or Schannel configuration changes that suppress OCSP/CRL validation. Correlate with execution of unsigned or suspiciously-signed binaries.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Exploitation — Crafted HTTP Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero UCs. This is the primary attack vector and must be detected at network layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (typical paths: /fapi/*, /admin, /sandbox, /api/) lacking authentication headers, containing command-like patterns (shell metacharacters: |, ;, ``, $(), &, >, etc.) in query parameters or POST bodies. Baseline: zero such requests pre-exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Process Execution — Unexpected Child Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection,' which must instantiate shell child processes. Article: 'execute unauthorized commands' → process telemetry hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FortiSandbox service processes (fortisandboxd, fsandboxd, etc.) spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh without corresponding API/UI action. Baseline: FortiSandbox should not spawn shells under normal operation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated API Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker.' Network boundary detection for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox IP:port lacking Authorization headers or valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints (port 8080, 8443, 4000 typical) missing Authorization or Session-ID headers. Alert if request count exceeds baseline per-source IP, or if source is external/untrusted.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' for command injection. Signature-based hunt for common injection patterns (pipe, semicolon, backticks) in request parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: HTTP requests to FortiSandbox containing payloads matching regex: (\||;|`|\$\(|&&|\|\|) in URL parameters or POST body. Correlate with 200-OK responses or error codes 500, 502 (command injection side effects).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19' + CISA KEV status implies immediate remediation required. Asset inventory hunt for unpatched FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset database for Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Cross-reference with patch management system; flag any instance with OS version < patch cutoff date (if available from vendor) or patch-date > 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Detect Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for detecting these malicious HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox services (ports 80, 443, 8080) for common OS command injection payloads (shell metacharacters: backticks, $(), |, &&, ;, newline characters). Correlate unauthenticated requests (no auth header or failed LDAP/local auth logs) with payloads targeting known FortiSandbox vulnerable endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect Unexpected Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute unauthorized commands' via command injection. Pipeline did not map execution phase of the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox parent processes (common parents: fortisandbox-server, fssandboxd, or web service context). Baseline legitimate child processes per environment and flag anomalies, especially shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe) or system utilities (curl, wget, nc) not typically spawned by FortiSandbox.

suggestion.title: Detect Authentication Bypass to FortiSandbox Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker' implies successful bypass of authentication controls. No UC generated for auth anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP 200/302 responses to FortiSandbox admin endpoints (/admin, /api, /dashboard) without prior successful authentication (no valid session token, API key, or LDAP bind event). Flag successful responses to these endpoints within 30 seconds of a failed auth attempt.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Indicator Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references CVE-2026-25089 as the exploit vector. Pipeline IOC section empty; this CVE should be a baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference asset inventory and vulnerability scanner output (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for FortiSandbox instances (all variants: on-premise, Cloud, PaaS) flagged with CVE-2026-25089. Prioritize publicly routable instances. Correlate with network telemetry to confirm whether instances have received inbound HTTP traffic from untrusted sources post-publication date (2026-07-16).

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection to FortiSandbox Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is the direct attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to known FortiSandbox endpoints (/api/, /cgi-bin/, /admin/) containing OS command injection metacharacters (semicolon, pipe, backtick, dollar-parenthesis, logical operators) in query strings or POST body, especially from unauthenticated sessions or with missing Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: 'execute unauthorized commands' directly implies shell/command execution spawned by the vulnerable process—no detection was generated for this execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service processes (PID match or parent process name) that execute interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) or contain shell metacharacters in command lines.

suggestion.title: Mass Reconnaissance for Exposed FortiSandbox Instances
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires public-facing FortiSandbox exposure; pipeline missed the reconnaissance phase preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple connection attempts to FortiSandbox signature ports (443, 8080, 8443, 8000) from external IPs, followed by successful HTTP requests containing probe/inject payloads, indicating active scanning and exploitation chains.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Anomalies to FortiSandbox (Malformed/Error Spikes)
suggestion.rationale: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' may trigger web server errors (4xx/5xx) or logging anomalies; no detection for reconnaissance indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spike in HTTP 400/403/500 responses to FortiSandbox endpoints, particularly those with unusual parameter encoding, binary payloads, or oversized request bodies—indicators of payload optimization and fuzzing.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Admin/API Endpoint Abuse Without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: 'public-facing application' and 'unauthenticated' imply attackers target management interfaces directly; no UC generated for auth bypass or direct API access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag direct access to known-sensitive FortiSandbox endpoints (/admin/, /api/v1/, /cgi-bin/monitor) from external IPs with absent or invalid session cookies, or HTTP methods not typically seen in normal admin workflows (e.g., OPTIONS, TRACE).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Inventory and Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: Article enumerates affected products: 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.' SOC must identify and prioritize vulnerable instances before federal patch deadline (2026-07-19).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset databases for installed FortiSandbox versions. Cross-reference with patch compliance baselines. Prioritize internet-facing or perimeter-exposed instances for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts Against FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Web-facing services must be monitored for malformed payloads characteristic of command-injection attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox services (ports 80, 443) for injection patterns in URI parameters, abnormal request sizes, suspicious headers, or 400/403 response clusters from single IP sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Web Service
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows attacker to 'execute unauthorized commands' post-injection. Process creation from web service accounts (e.g., FortiSandbox daemon processes) is anomalous and should be alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process spawning from FortiSandbox service accounts (cmd.exe, powershell, bash, wget, curl). Correlate timing with HTTP requests containing injection patterns. Flag any outbound network connections from child processes.

suggestion.title: Persistence Establishment Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: RCE via command injection typically leads to persistence attempts. Standard post-exploitation behavior for OS-level code execution vulnerabilities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox systems for creation of scheduled tasks, Windows services, cron jobs, or systemd units—especially those created by non-admin accounts or with timing correlating to exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiSandbox Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Successfully exploited FortiSandbox (especially Cloud/PaaS variants deployed in cloud or DMZ) serves as pivot point for lateral movement to internal systems or adjacent cloud infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections from FortiSandbox servers to internal subnets, domain controllers, credential stores, or other sensitive infrastructure. Monitor for DNS reconnaissance queries and failed authentication spikes from the compromised appliance.

suggestion.title: SQL injection in DIRAC FileCatalog checkDataset query parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'checkDataset function passes its datasets argument directly to the backend DB handler' and describes SQL injection vulnerability. No UC currently detects malformed or suspicious SQL patterns in FileCatalog queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FileCatalog/DatasetManager database audit logs for SQL queries on datasets table containing OR/UNION/DROP keywords or quote-escaping patterns in the datasets parameter. Correlate with subsequent eval() calls or process spawning from Tornado handler.

suggestion.title: eval() execution with user-controlled Python code from DIRAC database
suggestion.rationale: Article core vulnerability: 'passes the result to eval'. The pipeline's existing UCs hunt post-RCE indicators but miss the actual code execution vector. Application/runtime logs would show eval() being called with database-sourced strings.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt DIRAC application logs or Python audit logs for eval() or exec() calls where the argument originates from the FileCatalog database results. Correlate timing with SQL injection detection to isolate attacker-controlled code execution.

suggestion.title: Authenticated user privilege escalation via SQL injection to unauthenticated RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'authenticated user' as prerequisite. No UC detects account compromise + lateral SQL injection. Should correlate authentication logs with FileCatalog query anomalies to identify privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DIRAC service account authentication followed by unusual FileCatalog queries (large payloads, multi-statement, timing anomalies). Flag if normal user account performs admin-level FileCatalog API calls without corresponding privilege grant.

suggestion.title: DIRAC config file exfiltration post-RCE (credential theft)
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1552.001 but UC_101_2 only hunts file reads. Should also detect exfiltration (network writes) of dirac.cfg to C2 or external storage post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate UC_101_2 file reads of dirac.cfg with subsequent outbound network connections (DNS queries, HTTP POST, scp/sftp) from the affected DIRAC process context within 5-10 minutes.

suggestion.title: HTTP-based Command Injection to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—requires detection of malicious HTTP request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints containing command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax). Focus on requests from external IPs without valid authentication tokens. Baseline and alert on deviation from normal parameter usage.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute unauthorized commands'—must detect child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service or web worker context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag unexpected process execution (shells, utilities) spawned by FortiSandbox service account. Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; alert on deviation. Prioritize cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, reverse-shell indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV annotation means active exploitation in the wild—require IPS/WAF signatures even for patched systems to catch attack attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy network-layer signatures for CVE-2026-25089 exploitation attempts targeting known vulnerable FortiSandbox endpoints. Alert on payload matches regardless of patch status to detect attack reconnaissance or exploitation against unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Access Control Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access—should detect patterns consistent with bypassing authentication or targeting management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox logs for: successful connections lacking authentication headers, requests to administrative endpoints from non-whitelisted IPs, parameter fuzzying in logs, or HTTP 200/302 responses to requests that should require auth. Correlate timing with external scans.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Activity from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: After initial command execution, adversaries perform discovery/lateral movement—monitor for anomalous network and system activity originating from FortiSandbox host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network scanning (port/service enumeration) or credential enumeration originating from FortiSandbox IP. Detect lateral movement attempts (RDP, SMB, SSH) from FortiSandbox to internal hosts. Flag DNS queries for internal infrastructure from FortiSandbox process context.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Asset Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in `../_TEMPLATES.md#asset-exposure`' and provides CVE-2026-25089 as the substitution target. Pipeline generated no asset-discovery UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for exposed Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS instances accessible without authentication. Asset inventory by 2026-07-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox HTTP Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability...allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the attack vector itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints with command shell metacharacters (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), &&, ||) or base64-encoded payloads from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection 'execute unauthorized commands' — detection requires identifying shell processes spawned by the vulnerable service outside normal operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or sh spawned as children of Fortinet FortiSandbox processes. Flag any interactive shell or system utility execution outside defined sandbox contexts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Network Egress from Compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article severity 'crit' and CISA KEV status indicate active exploitation; injected commands typically establish C2 or download payload, creating detectable network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate timestamp of successful HTTP injection attempt with unexpected outbound connections from FortiSandbox instance (reverse shells, data exfiltration, payload downloads).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Application Logs: Injection Syntax Errors and Failed Commands

suggestion.title: Detect HTTP Requests to Exposed FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker' exploiting 'public-facing application' via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — asset exposure is the entry point. Pipeline acknowledged asset-exposure template but never instantiated it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints from internet-routable sources. Flag non-standard User-Agents, request payloads in headers/parameters, probing of undocumented endpoints, and scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect OS Command Injection Payloads in HTTP Traffic
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly described as 'OS command injection...via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — requires pattern-matching on injection metacharacters. Core attack vector but no detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request bodies and parameters for command-injection indicators (;, |, &&, ||, backticks, $(), %0A, %0D) targeting FortiSandbox endpoints. Alert on POST/PUT with unusual encodings.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Process Creation from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Successful injection results in 'execute unauthorized commands' — implying child process spawning from FortiSandbox service. Standard post-injection detection pipeline missed entirely despite clear execution phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts. Flag shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe), interpreters (perl, python), or utilities (curl, wget, nc) launched from appliance web service contexts.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exploitation Outbound Connections from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers achieve 'execute unauthorized commands' but no detection for what those commands *do* post-exploitation (callbacks, data exfil, lateral movement). Represents blind spot in attacker workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound network connections initiated by FortiSandbox processes to non-whitelisted destinations, non-standard ports, known-malicious IPs, or internal-only resources.

suggestion.title: Monitor FortiSandbox Application Logs for Injection Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Injection attempts often leave traces in application error logs (parse failures, exception stack traces, encoding errors). Article notes threat is 'observed exploited in the wild' — log signatures likely available but pipeline did not suggest application-log sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox application logs for HTTP parsing failures, command-execution exceptions, or unusual log levels coinciding with suspicious inbound requests. Correlate with network IDS/WAF alerts.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — implies exposed FortiSandbox instances are the ingress vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances responding to HTTP requests on default ports (8080, 443) from untrusted networks. Correlate against CVE-2026-25089 vulnerability scanner results. Priority is assets patched vs. unpatched within federal due date (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability...via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — implies detectable payload patterns in HTTP headers/body.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection metacharacters: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, &&, || in query parameters and POST bodies. Flag requests with shell escape sequences.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute unauthorized commands' as outcome — expect process spawning from FortiSandbox daemon/service contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts or daemon processes, especially shell interpreters (cmd.exe, bash, sh) or network utilities (curl, wget). Baseline normal FortiSandbox process trees.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Log Anomalies: Failed Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is unauthenticated; FortiSandbox logs should record failed/anomalous authentication patterns preceding exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application logs for high volumes of unauthenticated requests, HTTP 401/403 responses followed by 200 responses (auth bypass), or log entries indicating command-injection parsing errors or unexpected string escape sequences.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Violation: Lateral Movement from Compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE on FortiSandbox could enable lateral movement; article implies execution context is the appliance, not sandboxed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After exploitation, monitor for unexpected outbound connections from the FortiSandbox IP to internal network segments, especially to sensitive assets (domain controllers, data stores). Flag connections to ports 22, 3389, 445.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies three affected product variants (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) requiring urgent patch/remediation tracking; no asset-discovery UC generated despite CISA KEV urgency
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query network/vulnerability scanners for FortiSandbox instances on standard ports (typically 8080, 443). Cross-reference against patched inventory. Federal due-date enforcement requires completeness; patch-lag is the common failure mode.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is the initial-access foothold and must be hunted
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP logs for suspicious request patterns against FortiSandbox endpoints (e.g., unusual parameter encoding, command metacharacters in query strings, payload patterns known to trigger CVE-2026-25089). Absence of authentication headers in attack traffic is a key signal.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'execute unauthorized commands'—command-line execution is the execution phase and should be detected at process level when injection succeeds
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox web service or backend processes (e.g., FortiSandbox Java process launching cmd.exe, bash, or other shells). Baseline normal process trees first; injected commands typically appear as anomalous children.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries require asset-scanning; this UC bridges vulnerability scanner findings to incident response queue with federal deadline context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create high-priority alerts from vulnerability scanners matching CVE-2026-25089 against any host. Correlate with asset inventory to flag unpatched instances. Flag for immediate escalation with federal patch due-date (2026-07-19) as SLA anchor.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Access Log Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack delivery method: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—FortiSandbox application logs are the primary detection boundary for this unauthenticated vulnerability
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox HTTP access/error logs for payload indicators: request sizes exceeding baseline, non-standard HTTP methods, suspicious parameter formats, or error patterns consistent with injection failures (e.g., 500s following crafted requests). Baseline request patterns before and after patch application.

suggestion.title: External Remote Services Access to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies public-facing exploitation; if FortiSandbox is internet-exposed, external network sessions are a critical detection gap
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any successful HTTP/HTTPS connections to FortiSandbox instances from external/untrusted networks. Cross-reference with known-malicious ASNs and threat-intel feeds. High-confidence signal if external IPs attempt the injection payload and then spawn child processes.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Injection Patterns to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the exploitation vector and must be detectable via request payload inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox default ports (typically 8080/8443 or management interfaces) containing OS command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, &, ;) in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with failed-auth attempts preceding successful command execution.

suggestion.title: Unusual Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection via HTTP implies spawned child processes from the web service. Article specifies 'OS command injection' as the vulnerability mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process creation (cmd.exe, bash, sh, powershell) spawned by FortiSandbox service user/process context. Baseline normal FortiSandbox child processes and alert on anomalies, especially those involving network recon tools or reverse shells.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV explicitly requires vulnerability scanning correlation. Article references CVE-2026-25089 by exact ID for patch tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner results flagging CVE-2026-25089 against network exposure. Flag any FortiSandbox instances scanned with this CVE ID as critical until patch confirmation and deployment.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to FortiSandbox Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is triggered via unauthenticated HTTP requests. Pre-exploitation reconnaissance involves HTTP requests to exposed FortiSandbox management endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests from external IPs to known FortiSandbox management ports (8080, 8443, or vendor-default ports) where authentication is missing or bypassed. High volume from single source or across multiple sources suggests scanning/exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Network Exposure of FortiSandbox Appliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation against 'public-facing' assets. Article emphasizes unauthenticated attack surface requiring network accessibility.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Verify FortiSandbox appliances are not internet-routable on management ports. Hunt for inbound traffic from external/untrusted ASNs to FortiSandbox endpoints. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm firewall rules isolate this appliance appropriately.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL' and 'Anything in CISA KEV is *currently* being exploited.' Requires discovery of exposed FortiSandbox instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox appliances (Cloud, PaaS, on-prem) listening on HTTP/HTTPS ports exposed to untrusted networks. Correlate with patch status for CVE-2026-25089. Match against Shodan/Censys fingerprints for FortiSandbox HTTP response signatures.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox OS Command Injection via HTTP
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the core exploitation vector requiring detection at HTTP layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection payloads in parameters, POST bodies, headers (shell metacharacters: $, `, |, &, ;, newlines). Correlate with unauthenticated request patterns and anomalous source IPs.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Child Process Execution Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of 'execute unauthorized commands' manifests as unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service account—direct indicator of command injection success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes for FortiSandbox daemons (typically root or system-level service account). Alert on anomalous spawns: reverse shells, curl/wget, python, perl, nc, dd, or data exfiltration tools during exploit window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and 'Even if your scanners say "not vulnerable"... it's worth one quick check.' Detection must correlate scanner detection with unpatched inventory past federal due date 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate Nessus/Qualys/Tenable detection of CVE-2026-25089 against asset CMDB. Flag any FortiSandbox instance with version below [patched release] remaining unpatched after 2026-07-19. Correlate with active network exposure.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Request Sequences
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is unauthenticated-only; legitimate access requires auth. Article identifies unauthenticated attacker—detection should flag auth bypass or absence of valid credentials in requests to admin/API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor sequences of unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints: lack of Authorization header or session token → 401/403 response → follow-up request with command injection payload. Alert on any unauthenticated access to /admin, /api, /sandbox paths.

suggestion.title: POST to WordPress Core Endpoint Without Session
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'unauthenticated attackers'—exploitation requires malicious HTTP POST to WordPress core. Pipeline missed basic initial-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST requests to wp-admin/*, wp-includes/*, wp-login.php, or wp-json/* without valid WordPress authentication cookie or session token. Flag payloads containing base64 strings, PHP tags, or code-execution keywords like exec(), system(), shell_exec().

suggestion.title: Web Server Process Spawns Shell Interpreter
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'run code'—successful exploit spawns shell. Pipeline missed process-execution detection for www-data/apache executing bash/sh.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for apache2, nginx, php-fpm, or www-data process spawning /bin/bash, /bin/sh, /bin/perl, or /usr/bin/python. High fidelity if parent UID is unprivileged web user and child process includes command-line arguments indicative of reverse shell setup.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Creation in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: WordPress RCE exploitation installs backdoors—article text would detail payload delivery. Pipeline missed persistence-layer file-write detections to wp-content/uploads/ or wp-content/plugins/.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of .php, .phtml, or .php5 files in wp-content/uploads/, wp-content/plugins/, or /tmp/ by web-server process. Flag if filename contains encoded strings, random characters, or keywords like 'shell', 'backdoor', 'webshell'.

suggestion.title: wp-config.php Access by Web Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE leads to exfiltration of database credentials stored in wp-config.php. Pipeline missed credential-access file-read anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file reads of /var/www/html/wp-config.php (or equivalent WordPress root) by www-data or web process outside normal application initialization. Cross-correlate with outbound DNS/HTTP to detect exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Unusual HTTP 200 to Normally-Protected Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE implies single-request exploitation—anomalous HTTP 200 responses without prior session establish compromise. Pipeline missed response-code baselines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline HTTP response distribution per WordPress endpoint (wp-admin/, wp-login.php, REST API). Alert on sources with no prior successful 200 responses achieving 200 on protected endpoints; prioritize requests with suspicious User-Agent or referrer patterns.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation in WordPress Core
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly establishes SQL injection as the vector: 'Unauthenticated RCE in WordPress core...via SQL injection'. No detection UC generated despite clear adversarial action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web application logs for SQL syntax errors, UNION-based injection patterns, time-based blind SQL injection delays, or abnormal SQL keywords (DROP, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) in HTTP parameters. Correlate with successful HTTP 200 responses to identify exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via wp2shell Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'wp2shell' as the RCE mechanism but no execution-phase detection rule was generated. Pipeline missed the exploitation-to-execution bridge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual PHP process execution or shell spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe) initiated by web server user (www-data, apache, IUSR). Look for parent process of httpd/php-fpm spawning child shells, especially with suspicious command arguments or encoding (base64, gzip, obfuscation).

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Shell Access and Stabilization
suggestion.rationale: Successful RCE typically leads to reverse shell or web shell implantation. Article describes impact ('Patch now!') implying active compromise scenarios, but no post-exploitation detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to web-accessible WordPress directories (.../wp-content/, .../wp-admin/) with suspicious extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar) or embedded shells. Correlate outbound network connections from web server user to non-standard ports, especially in bursts post-HTTP-request.

suggestion.title: WordPress Version Enumeration Prior to Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated attackers typically enumerate WordPress version before targeting specific CVEs. Article severity and version-specific patch imply reconnaissance precedes exploitation, but no discovery-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect automated requests to WordPress version disclosure endpoints: /wp-includes/version.php, /readme.html, /?p=1, wp-json/wp/v2/users, or requests for multiple /wp-admin/*, /wp-content/* URLs from single source. Look for User-Agent patterns associated with scanner tools (sqlmap, burp, nikto).

suggestion.title: SQL Error-Based Information Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection exploitation typically triggers database errors revealing schema or version info. Article establishes SQL injection vector but no detection for verbose error responses that enable exploitation refinement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP responses containing SQL error messages (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MSSQL syntax) or database stack traces in response bodies. Correlate with requests containing SQL metacharacters (', ", --, /*, UNION). Alert on repeated error-returning requests from same source indicating iterative exploitation.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-RCE to System User
suggestion.rationale: RCE as web server user (limited privilege) often followed by privesc to root/SYSTEM. Article severity ('crit') and 'Patch now!' urgency suggest full system compromise risk, but pipeline missed privilege escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attempts to spawn privileged shells (sudo, su -c, runas) from web server user context, especially if successful (exit code 0). Monitor for kernel exploit signatures, CVE-based privesc payloads, or capabilities/permission changes on web server processes.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Post-Install Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'—delivery mechanism is post-install hooks in package.json or .npmrc. Pipeline captured nothing about package installation or script execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm/node processes spawning unusual child processes (PowerShell, cmd, curl, wget) immediately after package installation. Focus on post-install lifecycle events where node_modules scripts execute with parent=npm or parent=node.exe spawning unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: Blockchain-Based C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes 'Blockchain C2' as delivery mechanism—this is the malware's command channel. Pipeline failed to create detections for blockchain-routed traffic or contract queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RAT processes performing DNS lookups to blockchain nodes (Ethereum, Solana, or privacy-focused chains) or establishing connections to known blockchain RPC endpoints. Flag processes initiating HTTPS to blockchain explorers or smart-contract interaction patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Version Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often pivot on typosquatting or dependency confusion. Article references 'malicious Vite npm packages'—detection must cover installation anomalies and package metadata mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install commands for packages with names similar to popular Vite libraries, unusual version strings (pre-release tags from untrusted registries), or package.json modifications that enforce specific malicious versions via lock files.

suggestion.title: RAT Capability Indicators from Node.js Process
suggestion.rationale: Delivery mechanism is a RAT (Remote Access Trojan), yet no detections for RAT file operations, persistence, or exfiltration behaviors. Article confirms post-install unpacking into node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor node.exe or child processes for direct registry access, suspicious file writes to Startup folders, execution from temporary directories, or network connections to C2 addresses shortly after package installation. Cross-correlate process lineage: npm → node → suspicious binary.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: The attack vector is poisoned packages on npm registry—need telemetry on registry API calls, package metadata queries, or npm CLI using non-standard registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm CLI invocations with registry overrides (--registry flags pointing to attacker infrastructure), package.json referencing unusual Vite variants, or .npmrc files with non-standard authentication tokens. Flag installations from private/test registries during normal deployment workflows.

suggestion.title: Extraction and Decoding of Node Module Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Post-install scripts typically extract compressed or encoded payloads. Pipeline missed detection of file carving, archive extraction, or PE/shellcode decoding from within node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on archive utilities (7z, tar, unzip) or PowerShell decompression operators executed in node_modules context. Flag processes decoding Base64/hex-encoded blobs or executing inline PowerShell launched from package.json install phases.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes ServiceAccount Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet 'hunts for Kubernetes tokens.' Pipeline produced zero detection coverage for this attack vector, despite being explicit in the title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token or ~/.kube/config followed by network exfiltration. Flag non-kubelet processes accessing token paths. Correlate file read + outbound connection in <5min window to non-cluster IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud API Key Harvesting from Exposed AI Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'hunts exposed AI services for cloud keys.' No use case for reconnaissance of misconfigured LLM endpoints (HuggingFace, SageMaker, etc.) leaking credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning of AI model serving ports (8000, 8080, 5000) for environment variable leaks, metadata endpoints, or credential files. Flag requests to /.env, /config, /secrets, or AWS metadata service (169.254.169.254) from rotating source IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Exfiltrated Cloud Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential theft enables cloud account takeover. Zero detection for simultaneous credential use across geographies, unauthorized API calls with stolen keys, or anomalous principal behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API authentication using discovered credentials from IPs outside organization baseline or different regions within minutes of first use elsewhere. Flag calls to sensitive APIs (CreateAccessKey, DeleteUser, ModifyDBInstance) from compromised principals.

suggestion.title: Container Registry and Cloud Storage Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Kubernetes tokens grant access to container registries and storage. Article context implies targeting of ECR/ACR/GCR. No detection for registry scanning or secret enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ListRepositories, DescribeRepositories, ListImages from unrecognized principals or access denied patterns indicating brute-force repository enumeration. Flag GetAuthorizationToken calls followed by registry pulls.

suggestion.title: Secrets Manager Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised cloud keys provide access to Secrets Manager, Azure Key Vault, etc. No detection for mass secret retrieval or enumeration of secrets outside principal's historical scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on ListSecrets + GetSecretValue patterns from a principal showing no prior secret access. Alert on bulk secret retrieval (>5 secrets in <10min) or access to secrets tagged as 'prod' or 'critical'.

suggestion.title: NadMesh C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Botnet must beacon to C2. Article title references 'NadMesh' but pipeline extracted zero indicators. No domains, IPs, or behavioral signatures for botnet C2 defined.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS to NadMesh-attributed C2 domains (pending IOC feed). Detect DGA-like query patterns or certificates with known malicious issuers. Alert on port combinations or tunnel signatures consistent with botnet beaconing.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Code-Signing Certificate Usage
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on theft of code-signing certificates; detection of unexpected certificate issuers or serial numbers in process signature chains directly addresses the post-breach attack surface: 'Code-Signing Certificate Theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor executables signed with certificates not matching expected issuers (e.g., certificates bearing DigiCert serial ranges outside legitimate software publishers). Alert on code-signed binaries executed from temporary directories, user-writable paths, or unusual network shares. Cross-correlate with certificate revocation lists for known-stolen serials.

suggestion.title: DigiCert Certificate Store Access by Non-Administrative Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of DigiCert infrastructure implies theft from certificate stores; detecting unauthorized access to local or remote certificate repositories establishes credential-access phase: 'breach and code-signing certificate theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes outside the Windows Certificate Store management tools (certmgr.exe, mmc.exe with cert snapin) or key management services reading %APPDATA%\Microsoft\SystemCertificates or HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SystemCertificates. Flag native access to certificate private key material (PFX/P12 files) from non-service accounts.

suggestion.title: Compromise of DigiCert/Entrust Account Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'DigiCert Breach'; detection of compromised account activity or lateral movement from DigiCert infrastructure establishes initial-access and credential-access phases without requiring IOC specificity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual sign-in patterns to DigiCert and certificate authority portals: impossible travel, off-hours access, new device fingerprints, API key usage from unfamiliar IPs. Alert on bulk certificate issuance, revocation of legitimate certificates, or modification of certificate policies within a short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Malware Signed with Stolen Code-Signing Certificates
suggestion.rationale: Breach results in certificate theft specifically for signing malware; detection of signed PE files with anomalous metadata or from suspicious sources directly operationalizes the attack: 'GoldenEyeDog Subgroup Linked to...Code-Signing Certificate Theft.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement signature verification checks in EDR/XDR tooling: alert when a binary's code signature validates but does not match expected publisher metadata or when the issuing CA certificate is known-compromised. Flag signed binaries that trigger AV/YARA detections despite valid signatures (true positive + valid signature = defense evasion).

suggestion.title: Certificate-Based Persistence via Code-Signing
suggestion.rationale: Stolen certificates enable long-term malware deployment and updates without re-compromise; detection of persistence mechanisms leveraging code-signing certificates maps to the post-theft exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for signed executables in persistence locations (HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, startup folders, scheduled tasks). Alert on signed binaries with weak or invalid timestamps, self-signed certificates, or certificates issued to shell companies / regional variations of known publishers.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 HTTP Injection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — no UC captures HTTP payload patterns targeting FortiSandbox command injection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox API endpoints containing shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`) or common command injection payloads. Baseline legitimate API calls and alert on deviation from expected request morphology.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated API Access
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is explicitly unauthenticated; article states attacker requires no credentials. Missing UC for absence of auth headers or 401/403 bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox management/API endpoints that succeed (HTTP 200-299) without Authorization header, Bearer token, or session cookie. Correlate with response sizes indicating data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Process Command Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Injection leads to 'execute unauthorized commands'; article indicates execution happens post-exploitation. Need process-level detection of shell spawning from FortiSandbox parent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, bash, sh, or network device CLI spawned as child of FortiSandbox process (fsandbox, PID tracking). Establish baseline of legitimate child processes; flag unexpected shells or commands with redirection/pipes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet-Facing Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active wild exploitation; article notes 'public-facing application' risk. Standard asset-exposure hunt referenced but not implemented.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and external scanning feeds for FortiSandbox/FortiSandbox Cloud instances reachable on :80, :443, or API ports from internet. Cross-reference against patching status (due 2026-07-19); alert on exposed unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Sandbox Escape / Lateral Movement Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'improper isolation or compartmentalization' (title context); if command injection breaks sandbox boundary, need detection for processes accessing host resources outside sandbox scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect FortiSandbox processes accessing system files, registry, or network resources outside their expected sandbox scope (e.g., %WINDIR%, /etc, network share access). Flag privilege escalation attempts or file writes to sensitive directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Audit
suggestion.rationale: Federal remediation due 2026-07-19; standard CISA KEV workflow includes patch-gap hunt. Not surfaced as UC despite article stating compliance deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiSandbox instances across infrastructure and cross-reference against patch level. Flag instances where version < remediated build. Correlate with exposure findings to prioritize remediation risk.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet-Facing Asset Exposure (CISA KEV CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' as primary detection. Unauthenticated remote exploitation requires exposed assets: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances with inbound HTTP/HTTPS exposure from untrusted networks. Compare asset inventory against vulnerability scanner results; flag instances with unknown or pre-patch versions.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payloads to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly requires crafted HTTP requests: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Detection should hunt for command injection markers in requests to Fortinet endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search proxy/WAF logs for HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiSandbox hosts containing OS command metacharacters (pipe, backticks, $(), &&, |) in URI parameters or request bodies. Correlate with successful responses (200, 201) or response time anomalies.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Anomalous Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection directly leads to execution: 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands.' Detection must monitor for child processes spawned by FortiSandbox system processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of expected child processes for Fortinet sandbox services. Alert on unexpected spawning of shells, interpreters, or network tools (curl, wget, nc) from FortiSandbox processes, especially with low/system user context or from non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: Fortinet CVE-2026-25089 Patch Status Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date 2026-07-19 requires inventory of affected versions. Article lists three deployment models: 'FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query CMDB/asset system for all Fortinet product instances. Cross-reference against patched/unpatched status for CVE-2026-25089. Escalate any instance past federal due date or with unknown patch status.
