suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to /wp-admin/*, /wp-admin-ajax.php, or /wp-json/* endpoints lacking valid session cookie, authenticated token, or nonce validation. Establish baseline of legitimate public endpoints vs. admin-only paths. Alert if unauthenticated request triggers admin-level SQL queries or code execution paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes malicious Vite npm packages as attack entry point: 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'—no detection logic captured installation of compromised dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/ci commands installing packages matching known malicious hashes or from anomalous registries. Correlate with process spawn from node_modules/.bin executables and unexpected child processes (e.g., curl, powershell, cmd.exe) from npm postinstall hooks.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Network Communication from Build/Development Tools
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Blockchain C2' delivery mechanism—no detection for outbound connections to blockchain nodes or smart contract interaction from npm/Vite processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/TCP to known blockchain RPC endpoints (Ethereum, Solana, etc.) or blockchain explorer domains from node.js/npm processes. Flag DNS queries for blockchain infrastructure from build-time or runtime execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Process Execution from npm Module Cache with Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery implies code execution; article title indicates executable payload delivery via npm packages but no detection for anomalous process chains from node_modules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from node.js/npm with parent chain: npm → node → cmd/powershell/bash. Monitor for encoded command execution, base64 decoding, or curl/wget invocations from npm postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: Unusual File Writes or Data Exfiltration from Vite Build Output
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise of Vite packages could inject malicious code into build artifacts; no detection for suspicious file modifications in dist/ or exfiltration of source code/secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to package directories or build output locations containing network-accessible paths (e.g., http://, ftp://). Correlate with outbound network connections during build phases.

suggestion.title: npm Registry API Calls or Package Version Downgrades Post-Incident
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages identified in wild; no detection for lateral movement via compromised package versions or supply-chain recovery bypass attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry API calls (registry.npmjs.org) for suspicious package version queries or installations of pinned versions that bypass the malicious release. Track npm cache manipulation attempts.

suggestion.title: RAT Command Execution Patterns via Blockchain Wallet Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article describes RAT over blockchain C2—no detection for wallet addresses, smart contract calls, or decentralized command retrieval patterns that would indicate C2 callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET to blockchain explorer APIs or smart contract read operations with hex-encoded payloads. Correlate with RAT behavioral signatures (e.g., registry queries, process injection, persistence mechanisms).

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Access with Stolen Service Account Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Article centers on botnet harvesting 'Kubernetes Tokens'; this is the primary attack objective. Pipeline ignored K8s lateral-movement detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Kubernetes audit logs for API calls (get, list, create) against secrets, configmaps, and ClusterRoles using service account tokens from unexpected principals or mismatched namespaces. Alert on token usage from IP ranges outside organizational cloud infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Exposed AI Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies botnet 'hunts exposed AI services'; this is initial discovery phase. Pipeline omitted reconnaissance/scanning use cases entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid, sequential HTTP requests to common AI API paths (/v1/completions, /api/models, /.well-known/) from single source IP. Flag requests with high failure rates followed by successful token or credential endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Cloud Credential Exfiltration from Exposed Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'cloud keys' as primary loot; pipeline failed to model credential staging or extraction patterns from AI service instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk credential operations (iam:ListAccessKeys, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, az account get-access-token) originating from container/Lambda runtimes. Correlate with exfiltration patterns (large outbound connections, base64-encoded payloads in HTTP bodies).

suggestion.title: NadMesh Botnet Process Execution and C2 Callback
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline extracted zero process execution or command-and-control techniques despite article title explicitly naming a botnet. Execution and C2 are fundamental to any botnet campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for process spawning with CLI tools (curl, wget) or script interpreters executing HTTP requests to known C2 infrastructure. Alert on DNS queries with high-entropy subdomains or unusual destinations from container/Kubernetes nodes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Service Account or IAM Key Generation
suggestion.rationale: Article targets 'cloud keys'; pipeline missed detection for synthetic token generation or export outside normal provisioning workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service account token creation or kubeconfig export from running containers, requests to cloud provider STS endpoints from unexpected principals, or credential file reads from shared /tmp directories.

suggestion.title: Code-Signed Executable with Revoked DigiCert Certificate
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Code-Signing Certificate Theft'—pipeline must detect execution of binaries signed by compromised DigiCert certs on CRL.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where parent image has valid code signature from DigiCert (CN or thumbprint) AND cert serial is in revocation list OR cert timestamp falls within theft window. Cross-reference against trusted application baseline to reduce FP on intentionally-revoked legitimate software.

suggestion.title: Unusual Certificate Store Access or Export
suggestion.rationale: Breach narrative involves certificate theft from DigiCert systems—detect anomalous access to certificate stores, export tools, or key material repositories that precedes the compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of certmgr.exe, certutil.exe, or OpenSSL with parameters indicating cert export (e.g., -exportPFX, -exportCert, exportkey) outside change-control windows. Monitor for mass extraction or enumeration of certificates on DigiCert-associated systems.

suggestion.title: GoldenEyeDog Subgroup Infrastructure Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'GoldenEyeDog Subgroup' by name—pipeline must surface this actor name and associate known C2/exfil infrastructure with detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest GoldenEyeDog IOC feeds (if available via public reporting) and alert on network connections to known group infrastructure from any internal host. Flag DNS queries to domains associated with certificate distribution or malware C2.

suggestion.title: DigiCert System Lateral Movement and Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Certificate theft from DigiCert implies attacker gained elevated access within their infrastructure—detect network behavior and privilege escalation tactics typical of supply-chain targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Internal to DigiCert-like PKI environments, alert on: valid-account abuse (multiple failed then successful logins), RDP/SSH access to certificate-authority-tier systems from unexpected networks, enumeration of domain admins or certificate-store permissions.

suggestion.title: Signed Malware Distribution via Compromised Certificate Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article core threat is malware distribution using stolen code-signing certs—detect infection attempts using binaries with valid but suspicious signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate malware detections with code-signature metadata: if executable carries DigiCert signature but file hash is NOT in legitimate software whitelist and signature cert issuer date post-compromise, flag as suspicious. Combine with delivery vector (phishing, watering hole, etc.).

suggestion.title: Certificate Revocation Activity Spike on DigiCert-Issued Certs
suggestion.rationale: DigiCert will revoke stolen certificates—sudden mass revocation events or emergency CRL updates are a leading indicator of compromise scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CRL update frequency and revocation count from DigiCert. Alert if revocation rate anomalously increases or if previously-trusted certificate serials appear in CRL. Cross-check against internal systems that may have cached and are still using the revoked certs.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Exposed Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — establishes that public-facing FortiSandbox instances are the attack surface and CISA KEV means exploitation is already active.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for CVE-2026-25089 matches against all FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Segment by internet exposure and patch status. Alert on any unpatched exposed instances with federal due date of 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection' exploited via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — attack requires injection payloads in HTTP parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox administrative or API endpoints containing OS command injection indicators: shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `&&`, backticks, `$()`) in URL parameters or POST bodies, especially when source is external.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution on FortiSandbox Host
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation results in actual OS command execution on the appliance — post-injection telemetry would show spawned processes outside normal FortiSandbox operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox appliances for unexpected child process spawning from the FortiSandbox application user context, unusual command-line arguments, or execution of shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd) by processes that do not normally spawn them.

suggestion.title: Anomalous HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Services
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated HTTP-based exploitation implies attackers can reach the service over the network and submit payloads — detection should capture the reconnaissance and attack phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate HTTP requests to FortiSandbox instances (admin IPs, regional patterns). Alert on requests from unexpected geolocations, unusual request rates, malformed or oversized payloads, or requests to non-standard ports/paths attempting to trigger the vulnerability.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — this is the primary attack vector and must be detectable at the network/proxy layer before command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox management endpoints (typically port 8443, 9001) for HTTP/HTTPS requests with suspicious payloads, unusual parameter combinations, or command-injection-like encodings. Flag requests from unexpected source IPs or with rapid request bursts from new sources.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution on FortiSandbox Host
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows...execute unauthorized commands' — endpoint logs should capture unexpected process spawns from the FortiSandbox service/application user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox process context for child process execution, especially system commands (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell). Establish baseline of expected processes and alert on anomalies. Review FortiSandbox application logs for command injection error messages or unexpected interpreter invocations.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status indicates active wild exploitation; prerequisite for T1190 is that the target is network-accessible. Must identify all FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances accessible from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints; cross-reference with network ACLs, firewall rules, and external port scans to identify which instances are internet-facing or accessible from untrusted network segments. Alert on any newly exposed FortiSandbox instances.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Payload Detection in FortiSandbox Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — the malicious requests themselves may have detectable signatures (command injection patterns, encoding attempts, suspicious parameter values).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy WAF rules or proxy-based content inspection to detect command-injection payloads targeting FortiSandbox endpoints (e.g., backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes, shell metacharacters in request parameters). Establish allowlist of legitimate request patterns if FortiSandbox is in production.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Remediation Verification
suggestion.rationale: Federal patch due date is 2026-07-19 (published 2026-07-16, 3-day window). Must verify all FortiSandbox instances are patched to post-remediation version prior to deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run vulnerability scanner against all FortiSandbox endpoints to confirm CVE-2026-25089 is not present (patched version). Cross-reference patch management logs to confirm patches were deployed and verified before 2026-07-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP requests with injection payloads targeting FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—the exploit surface is unauth HTTP access with malicious payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiSandbox admin/API endpoints (destination ports 80/443/8080/8443, Host headers matching FortiSandbox) that lack valid session cookies or Authorization headers AND contain command-injection signatures: backticks, $(), semicolons, pipe characters, or unusual URL encoding in query/body payloads. Correlate source IPs across multiple requests.

suggestion.title: Child process execution spawned by FortiSandbox service processes
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection' enabling 'execution of unauthorized commands'—injected payloads will spawn unexpected processes under the vulnerable service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag shell interpreters (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) or unexpected utilities spawned as children of FortiSandbox worker/daemon processes without legitimate parent command-line context. Alert especially on high-privilege execution (SYSTEM, root) from HTTP service contexts.

suggestion.title: Network exposure of FortiSandbox instances without authentication controls
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability requires 'unauthenticated attacker'—prerequisite: identifying internet-facing FortiSandbox deployments accessible without valid credentials, especially those detected on public IP ranges or without WAF/reverse-proxy protection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory all FortiSandbox instances (product names: FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) on open ports 80/443/8080/8443. Cross-check authentication logs for successful logins from unauthenticated sessions (session ID not tied to valid credentials). Alert on any instances directly internet-facing without IP whitelisting or WAF interception.

suggestion.title: HTTP error spikes and malformed request patterns preceding exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specially crafted HTTP requests'—scanning/fuzz attempts by attackers will generate 400/500 errors and request anomalies before successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox endpoints for abnormal 400 Bad Request / 500 Internal Server Error rates. Alert on clusters of malformed requests (oversized payloads, invalid encoding, truncated headers) from single sources followed within minutes by successful authentication or process execution events.

suggestion.title: Outbound command-and-control or lateral movement connections from compromised FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Successful command injection grants OS-level RCE—attacker will use this to establish persistence or pivot. Article establishes attacker control over command execution but doesn't detail post-exploitation indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from FortiSandbox system IPs to external IPs or high-numbered ports. Alert on DNS queries for known C2 domains, connections to ASNs not on business whitelist, or beaconing patterns. Correlate with inbound exploitation attempts to identify successful compromise chains.

suggestion.title: Anomalous process behavior and resource exhaustion post-command-injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: attacker can 'execute unauthorized commands'—successful injection will manifest as unexpected processes, resource anomalies, or state changes in FortiSandbox system/performance logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox appliance syslog and performance data for unexpected process names, CPU/memory spikes from HTTP service, unusual CLI command execution in appliance shell, or file modifications outside maintenance windows. Alert on fortimanager CLI usage from HTTP service context.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero exploitation detection logic for this primary attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox instances (ports 8000, 8443, or administrative endpoints) for payloads containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, `), command substitution patterns, or encoding bypasses targeting command parameters. Alert on requests lacking authentication tokens or API keys.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Child Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection (article) implies shell execution. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection. Expected: predictable child processes; unexpected: cmd.exe, powershell, /bin/sh spawned by Fortinet services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes from FortiSandbox daemons. Flag unexpected shell spawns with high-risk keywords (whoami, id, curl, wget, nc, bash) or unusual working directories.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Vulnerability Scanner Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal due date 2026-07-19; article: 'Fortinet FortiSandbox [versions unspecified]'. Pipeline should include patch-status validation, not just exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate FortiSandbox instances via port scan (8000, 8443) or service fingerprinting. Cross-check versions against CVE-2026-25089 affected range. Prioritize unpatched instances; validate patch application dates vs. federal deadline.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Authentication Bypass Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Attack is unauthenticated (article). Pipeline omitted auth-layer detection. Look for requests circumventing session checks, missing credential validation, or default credential reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints that bypass or lack expected auth headers (Authorization, X-Auth-Token, session cookies). Correlate missing auth with suspicious payloads or admin endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Application Error Log Spike
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts generate errors. Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' implies parsing failures, exceptions, or unexpected behavior logged by FortiSandbox.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox logs for sudden spikes in errors containing 'command', 'injection', 'syntax', 'parse', or security-related keywords. Correlate timing with inbound HTTP scanning or exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploitable by 'unauthenticated attacker' via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—exposure to untrusted networks is prerequisite. Pipeline referenced standard asset-exposure template but generated no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox/FortiSandbox Cloud/PaaS instances accessible from internet. Query network telemetry, vulnerability scanner, and CMDB for instances running vulnerable versions on internet-routable interfaces. Prioritize instances with inbound access from external IP ranges on typical Fortinet ports (8000, 8080, 8443, 443).

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability...via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No detection hypothesis for payload indicators was generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox for command injection signatures: shell metacharacters (|, ;, &&, ||, backtick, $()), null bytes, and non-ASCII payloads in query parameters and POST bodies. Correlate successful 200/302 responses with anomalous process execution or error output in appliance logs. Flag requests with excessively long parameters (>2048 chars) to management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'execute[s] unauthorized commands' via injection. No behavioral detection for SYSTEM-level process spawning (bash, sh, cmd, wget, curl) on vulnerable appliances was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox instances, flag process creation spawned by Fortinet management daemons that invoke shells or dangerous utilities (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell, curl, wget, nc). Correlate timing of process execution with inbound HTTP requests and 5xx-then-2xx response sequences indicating failed-then-successful injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-19. Standard due-diligence detection should verify FortiSandbox versions are current; pipeline did not generate inventory/compliance check.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and CMDB for FortiSandbox instances running versions prior to vendor patch release. Identify instances exposed to untrusted networks via network telemetry or external DNS/TLS records. Alert on any CRIT/CVSS≥9 unpatched instances past the federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Management
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as attack delivery mechanism. Pipeline did not generate detection for HTTP-layer anomalies (headers, methods, encoding) that might bypass WAF/IDS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox using non-standard methods (CONNECT, TRACE, PATCH, DELETE) or malformed headers (Content-Length mismatch, incomplete TLS handshake, chunked encoding abuse). Flag requests with unicode/UTF-8 encoding bypasses in path or query strings. Correlate with 5xx appliance responses followed by authentication/authorization bypass indicators in logs.

suggestion.title: Patch inventory: FortiSandbox fleet status for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal due-date 2026-07-19 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'—vulnerability scanner queries are mandatory for CISA KEV. Article explicitly names Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query patch/version status across Fortinet FortiSandbox instances. Flag any unpatched or pre-patch-release versions. Cross-correlate with network exposure scans (external IP, port 8080/8443 accessibility) to identify exploitable assets.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiSandbox appliance endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is the external attack surface. Typical endpoints: management console, API, sandbox telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/S traffic to known FortiSandbox endpoints (commonly :80, :443, :8080, :8443) for requests lacking standard authorization headers (Authorization, Cookie) or originating from unexpected source networks. Correlate with 4xx rejection codes and upstream alert triggers.

suggestion.title: Command injection payloads in HTTP parameters to Fortinet endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' containing injection vectors. WAF signatures and proxy logs will show shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, backticks, $()) in query/POST bodies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox appliances with payloads containing shell escape characters, command separators (semicolon, pipe, &&), command substitution (backticks, $()), or wildcard operators. Cross-match against known FortiSandbox endpoint patterns.

suggestion.title: OS command execution spawned from FortiSandbox process context
suggestion.rationale: If unauthenticated HTTP request successfully injects commands, the FortiSandbox service will spawn shell processes (cmd.exe, bash, sh). Article describes RCE capability: 'execute unauthorized commands'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent-child process spawning where FortiSandbox daemons (fortisandboxd, sandbox-related processes) create command shells (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, /bin/sh, /bin/dash). Inspect child process command-line for injection artifacts, reverse shells, or credential theft commands.

suggestion.title: Network exposure of FortiSandbox to untrusted networks
suggestion.rationale: T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' presumes internet-facing appliance. Article does not specify segmentation; asset-exposure validation is prerequisite to risk quantification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan internal FortiSandbox instances for routes to Internet or DMZ. Flag appliances accessible from public IP space on ports 80, 443, 8080, 8443, or custom API ports. Validate firewall ACLs restrict access to trusted admin subnets only.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No UC generated despite clear initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox instances (ports 8000, 8080, or management endpoints) for HTTP POST/GET requests with suspicious command patterns in URI or payloads. Baseline normal administration traffic; flag requests from non-admin sources attempting to inject shell metacharacters (;, |, &&, `, $()) in HTTP parameters.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute unauthorized commands'—explicit command-execution phase. Pipeline generated no execution-phase hunts despite clear subprocess/shell activity post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox appliances, detect child processes spawned from the sandbox daemon or web service (e.g., FortiSandbox app pool) with parent process != expected binary. Flag cmd.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash, or wget/curl launched unexpectedly with unusual argument patterns (curl exfiltration, reverse-shell commands).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article title is in CISA KEV ('observed exploited in the wild'); implies exposed instances. Recommendations note 'standard asset-exposure hunt' but no inventory UC was generated to identify externally-reachable FortiSandbox instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results, SHODAN/Censys data, and passive DNS for FortiSandbox ports (typically 8000, 8080, management ports) reachable from untrusted networks. Identify instances with no authentication bypass mitigations (WAF rules, IP allowlists, VPN requirement) and prioritize patching.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Parameter Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as delivery method but no payload signature or parameter-inspection UC generated. Missing tactical detection for the actual exploitation craft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request payloads to FortiSandbox APIs/management endpoints for command-injection payloads: shell metacharacters in query strings or POST bodies, base64-encoded commands, or nested quoting patterns (e.g., `|(echo ...), $(command)). Correlate with non-200 responses or subsequent process spawning.

suggestion.title: Patched vs. Unpatched FortiSandbox Instance Drift
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-07-19. No UC to detect instances still running vulnerable versions post-patch-due-date. Critical for compliance and post-breach hunting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate FortiSandbox appliances and cross-check version numbers against CVE-2026-25089 patch threshold. Flag any instance still running pre-patch builds after the federal due date (2026-07-19). Prioritize immediate incident response triage on these systems given active KEV exploitation.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Fortinet FortiSandbox Instances (CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS' as affected products; CISA KEV status means active exploitation. Asset discovery is foundational.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for processes/services matching 'fortisandbox' or 'fmg' (Fortinet management) in your environment. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data to identify exposed instances. This is a time-critical hunt given the 2026-07-19 federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: HTTP Anomalies to FortiSandbox Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—direct call for HTTP-layer detection on the management port.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to known FortiSandbox management ports (typically 8001, 8443) for malformed requests, command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, $() subshell syntax), or requests from untrusted source IPs. Establish baseline of legitimate admin traffic first.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands'—this is post-exploitation detection for successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services (e.g., fmgfscaler, fmgdvm, sandbox processes) for suspicious command-line activity: shell invocations (cmd.exe, bash, sh), script interpreters, or network tools. High fidelity signal: any process spawning outside the expected FortiSandbox service account.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing FortiSandbox Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires active exploitation; T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is explicitly applicable. Article implies web-accessible instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify FortiSandbox instances reachable from untrusted networks or the internet. Query firewall/proxy logs for inbound connections to FortiSandbox management ports from external IP ranges. Cross-reference with asset inventory to flag externally accessible instances as critical.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to FortiSandbox APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker'—directly signals a detection requirement for auth-bypass or unauthenticated API calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox application logs and HTTP access logs for requests to sensitive endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, /management/*) that return 200/201 responses without valid authentication headers (missing/invalid session tokens, JWT, or API keys). Spike in unauthenticated successful requests is indicator of exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Craft HTTP Injection Attempts to FortiSandbox Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox URLs (Cloud, on-prem, PaaS instances) with malformed parameters, command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), env var injection), or abnormally high request rates from single source. Baseline on normal FortiSandbox management traffic.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution Following FortiSandbox HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands.' Pipeline did not suggest detection of post-exploitation command execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox process parent/child execution chains. Flag unexpected child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services (fortisandbox.exe, fssb, or cloud agent processes) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, powershell, sh, bash) especially if preceded by recent HTTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Exposure and Asset Inventory Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV requires federal remediation by 2026-07-19; asset-exposure detection is canonical ('Substitute this CVE wherever the template references `<CVE>`'). Pipeline supplied no asset-discovery UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross inventory against vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-25089 in Fortinet FortiSandbox (any flavor: on-prem, Cloud, PaaS). suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes accessing crash-report directories outside standard system/security software. Monitor for bulk file reads, archive operations (tar/zip), or upload via curl/python to exfil crash data.

suggestion.title: LaunchAgent Persistence Registration from Malware Process Lineage
suggestion.rationale: Stealer malware persists via LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon. CrashStealer's two-stage pattern (dropper→payload) suggests post-exploit persistence is likely, though not explicit in truncated article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .plist creation/modification in ~/Library/LaunchAgents linked to dropper parent process. Alert on LaunchAgent Label pointing to /tmp, /var/tmp, or recently-executed unsigned binaries.

suggestion.title: Gatekeeper Trust Control Subversion: Revoked or Malicious Certificates
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'notarized dropper to pass Gatekeeper checks.' Detection must identify certificates associated with CrashStealer family, revoked notarization records, or certificate use outside known developer scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build IOC list of certificates / notarization records linked to CrashStealer. Cross-reference code-signing data on process execution; alert if signature is valid but issuer/developer ID enters threat intel blacklist or shows behavioral anomalies (unusual runtime, network, or FS access).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Crash Data via Outbound Network Tunnel
suggestion.rationale: CrashStealer implies exfiltration. Detect unusual outbound network traffic from malware process lineage to non-Apple infrastructure, especially bulk transfers or encrypted tunnels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from CrashStealer process and descendants to domains outside apple.com or known CDNs. Alert on high-volume data transfers, persistent tunnels, or connections to known C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-25089. No UC provided for positive scan results or asset-exposure correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-25089 on any Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or PaaS instance. Correlate with inventory to track unpatched systems. Escalate any findings after Federal due date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'. No detection for anomalous HTTP patterns to FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances for command-injection indicators: shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), cmd substitution syntax, unusual parameter values in unauthenticated endpoints. Baseline normal API usage and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Post-Injection OS Command Execution on FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article outcome is 'execute unauthorized commands'. Detect abnormal process creation or shell invocation on compromised FortiSandbox hosts post-injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning or shell commands (bash, sh, cmd.exe) on FortiSandbox appliances, especially with elevated privileges. Flag commands inconsistent with sandbox operations (outbound connections, file exfiltration, enumeration).

suggestion.title: Internet-Facing FortiSandbox Appliance Exposure
suggestion.rationale: T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' combined with CISA KEV active exploitation. Verify no FortiSandbox instances are exposed to internet or untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and external scanning (Shodan, Censys) to identify all Fortinet FortiSandbox hosts and confirm none are internet-routable. Alert if any management or API port (443, 8443, custom) is publicly accessible.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Patch Deployment Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Article sets Federal patch deadline 2026-07-19. No UC for tracking patch application or post-deadline compliance verification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track patch status for CVE-2026-25089 across all FortiSandbox assets. Alert if any system remains unpatched after Federal due date. Correlate patch install logs with baseline inventory to ensure 100% coverage; escalate gaps to compliance team.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states this is CISA KEV (actively exploited in the wild) and references 'canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...#asset-exposure]'. The template should be instantiated with CVE-2026-25089 per the article's own instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner data and asset inventory for FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Alert on any system flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089, and cross-check patch levels against 2026-07-19 federal due date.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—this is a direct attack surface requiring behavioral detection of injection payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (ports commonly 8080, 8443, or 80/443 for cloud/PaaS variants) for command injection patterns in parameters: shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax ($(...),$(...), backticks), path traversal sequences, or OS-specific payloads.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Command Execution on FortiSandbox Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows unauthorized commands' to execute. Successful exploitation will manifest as unexpected processes spawned from network-sourced context rather than administrative console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous child process spawning under FortiSandbox service contexts (fortisandbox, sandbox daemon) where parent process indicates network origin (HTTP service, reverse shell handles) or unexpected command-line arguments containing encoded commands or shell invocations.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Post-Remediation for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and federal agencies required to remediate by 2026-07-19; compliance hunt ensures patched state was verified post-deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After 2026-07-19, verify all FortiSandbox assets report patched version covering CVE-2026-25089. Flag any instance still vulnerable post-due-date as either unpatched (remediation failure) or misconfigured (false-negative scanner result).

suggestion.title: WordPress Core Exploitation via wp2shell Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'WordPress Core Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code'—explicit exploitation of public-facing application. Pipeline extracted zero initial-access indicators or exploitation vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress installations for wp2shell exploitation payloads. Detect POST/GET requests to vulnerable WordPress endpoints from unauthenticated sources that receive 200 responses. Alert on requests containing code-execution indicators, shell metacharacters, or command-injection patterns in parameters targeting WordPress core.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Malicious WordPress Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'Run Code' without authentication—explicit execution capability. No execution-phase detection use cases were generated despite clear RCE impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate web server access logs showing wp2shell exploitation attempts with process creation events showing shell interpreters or command executors spawned under web server process identity (www-data, apache, nginx, IIS AppPool). Detect anomalous parent-child relationships and unexpected outbound connections from web server processes.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawning from Web Server
suggestion.rationale: RCE inherently implies code execution and process spawning under web server context. Pipeline missed execution-layer behavioral detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes created by web server processes (apache2, httpd, nginx, w3wp.exe) spawning command interpreters (/bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Flag unexpected file modifications, network connections, or privilege escalation attempts from web server worker processes post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection in Unauthenticated WordPress Request
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'SQL injection' as the attack vector. Pipeline emitted zero use cases despite this being the primary initial-access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress installations (wp-admin, wp-login.php, public endpoints) for SQL metacharacters and UNION/SELECT payloads in unauthenticated requests. Baseline normal WordPress query patterns and alert on syntax-like strings (OR 1=1, SLEEP(), stacked queries) in GET/POST parameters from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Command Execution Following Web Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated RCE outcome. Pipeline missed detection linking HTTP exploitation attempts to child process spawning from web-server user context (php-fpm, apache2 child).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious inbound HTTP requests (SQL injection patterns, encoded payloads) against ProcessCreated events spawned from WordPress application processes within 5 seconds. Alert on cmd.exe, /bin/bash, or /bin/sh children from php or httpd parent PIDs in web-server context.

suggestion.title: WordPress Core File Modification or Web Shell Creation
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE, attackers typically persist via web shells or core-file modification. Article implies exploitation leads to sustained access but pipeline generated no persistence-detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification in wp-content/, wp-admin/, or wp-includes/ directories with .php, .phtml, .php5 extensions outside standard deployment windows. Correlate with process execution or HTTP requests to newly created files; flag inline PHP scripts in legitimate WordPress directories.

suggestion.title: Database Schema Enumeration via Web Application
suggestion.rationale: SQL-injection RCE often involves attacker probing database structure (information_schema, sys tables). Pipeline provided no detection for reconnaissance queries through database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for SELECT from information_schema, mysql.user, or sys tables originating from WordPress application user. Alert on HIGH query volume or schema enumeration patterns (SHOW TABLES, SELECT table_name FROM...) following exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Activity from Compromised WordPress Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE typically enables C2 callback or data exfiltration. Article describes unauthenticated code execution but pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation network anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound TCP/UDP connections initiated by php-fpm or apache2 child processes to non-standard ports (not 80/443) or to IPs not in WordPress CDN/plugin-update whitelists. Correlate with timeframe following SQL injection exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation with Blockchain-Based C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes seven malicious Vite npm packages delivering a RAT via blockchain C2. Should detect anomalous npm installs followed by outbound blockchain/cryptocurrency network traffic. Phrase: 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages Use Blockchain C2 to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install operations (especially for 'vite' package variants) followed within seconds by process spawning network connections to known blockchain nodes or cryptocurrency mining pools. Correlate npm package names against threat intel; flag post-install JavaScript/Node.js child processes making cryptographic or P2P network calls.

suggestion.title: npm Post-Install Script Execution Spawning RAT-Like Process Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Malicious npm packages exploit post-install hooks to execute attacker-controlled code and drop a RAT. Should detect obfuscated or suspicious script execution during package installation. Phrase: 'malicious Vite npm Packages... to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm install lifecycle events (postinstall, preinstall scripts) that spawn child processes with network connectivity, file write activity to $HOME/.cache or %TEMP%, or execution of base64-decoded payloads. Track process parent-child chain from npm → node → unexpected binaries.

suggestion.title: Outbound Blockchain/Cryptocurrency Network Traffic from Development Toolchain
suggestion.rationale: RAT uses blockchain for C2, an unusual vector. Development machines running npm should not initiate cryptocurrency wallet queries, blockchain node syncs, or DNS lookups for mining pools. Phrase: 'Blockchain C2'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound TCP/UDP to known cryptocurrency blockchain RPC endpoints (Ethereum, Bitcoin, Monero RPC ports), blockchain explorers, or mining pool domains originating from npm, Node.js, or build-tool processes on non-infrastructure hosts.

suggestion.title: Vite Package Registry Typosquatting or Version Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malicious 'Vite npm Packages' — suggests either typosquatting the legitimate Vite package or compromised versions. Should flag registry lookups for variants or unusual version jumps. Phrase: 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry manifest downloads for package name similarities to 'vite' (vite-cli, vite2, vite-builder, etc.) and flag installations of versions with anomalous timestamps, unusual publisher accounts, or mismatched dependency graphs.

suggestion.title: RAT Beacon Initialization from npm Package Context
suggestion.rationale: RAT must initialize after installation. Look for process spawning, registry/file modifications, persistence mechanisms, or credential harvesting originating from npm post-install. Phrase: 'to Deliver a RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm/Node.js child processes that modify startup locations (registry Run keys, cron jobs, ~/.bashrc), write to ~/.ssh, enumerate system users, or spawn WMI/PowerShell commands for reconnaissance post-installation.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript in npm Package Payloads
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery via npm requires evasion of static analysis. Should detect base64, ROT13, or minified JavaScript hiding malicious logic in package tarballs or install scripts. Phrase: implicit in 'malicious packages deliver RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package postinstall scripts for high entropy strings, base64-encoded buffers, eval() calls, dynamic require statements, or character-code constructs that decode to network I/O or system commands.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Reconnaissance by NadMesh Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes botnet actively hunts 'exposed AI services'—indicating discovery/scanning phase targeting misconfigured cloud deployments. Title phrase: 'hunts exposed AI services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for scanning patterns against common AI service ports/endpoints (LLM APIs, model registries) from single or coordinated sources, combined with HTTP 200/403 responses indicative of service enumeration. Correlate with known NadMesh C2 if available.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes Token/API Key Exfiltration Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states botnet targets 'Kubernetes tokens' and 'cloud keys.' Title phrase: 'for Cloud Keys and Kubernetes Tokens.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious reads of service account tokens from /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/ or environment variable exfiltration. Flag API calls retrieving token secrets, especially from non-service accounts or unusual IPs.

suggestion.title: Cloud Provider Credential Store Querying
suggestion.rationale: Attack objective includes harvesting 'cloud keys'—requires querying credential stores, secrets managers, or environment configs. Implied by article scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect enumeration of IAM roles, secrets manager API calls, or environment variable reads within containers. Flag patterns querying multiple credential types in short time windows or from unexpected principals.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command & Control Communication (NadMesh)
suggestion.rationale: Botnet infrastructure must establish C2 to coordinate scanning and exfiltration. No C2 domains, IPs, or ports identified despite critical severity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NadMesh beacon traffic signatures (if known), unusual DNS queries to C2 infrastructure, or outbound connections from compromised containers to non-standard ports. Correlate with botnet IOC feeds.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Kubernetes Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Post-compromise, stolen K8s tokens enable lateral movement across cluster workloads and namespaces. Article implies token use for impact/persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API calls authenticated by service account tokens from unusual sources (external IPs, different clusters). Alert on cross-namespace API access or RBAC policy modifications using stolen credentials.

suggestion.title: Code-Signing Certificate Abuse – DigiCert Breach Window
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links GoldenEyeDog to 'code-signing certificate theft' from DigiCert; pipeline extracted zero detection use cases despite this being the *core attack vector*. Need to detect binaries signed with certificates issued during compromise window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binary execution where code-signing certificate issuer=DigiCert AND certificate serial within known-compromised batch AND signature timestamp during breach window (if known). Cross-reference against legitimate software publishers to isolate malware abuse of stolen certs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DigiCert Certificate Issuance Activity
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain breach implies unauthorized certificate requests or issuance from DigiCert infrastructure. Pipeline missed detecting anomalous cert-generation activity that typically precedes theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag certificate issuance requests from non-standard DigiCert user accounts, batch issuance of code-signing certs for unregistered organizations, or cert generation outside normal business hours if audit data available.

suggestion.title: GoldenEyeDog C2 or Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes breach to threat actor by name; pipeline extracted zero actor intelligence or associated infrastructure IOCs (domains, IPs, ASNs). Command-and-control communication should be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Once actor infrastructure is published in threat reports, correlate network logs for beacon activity to known GoldenEyeDog C2 domains/IPs. Prioritize TLS cert validation anomalies (cert pinning failures, unexpected CAs).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Lateral Movement in Certificate Authority Environment
suggestion.rationale: DigiCert breach implies attacker moved laterally within their environment to reach cert-signing infrastructure. Pipeline missed defense-evasion and lateral-movement techniques typical of supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for logons to DigiCert-infrastructure systems from unusual geographies, off-hours, or using delegated credentials. Look for lateral movement using pass-the-ticket or overpass-the-hash post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Stolen Certificate Authority Credential Usage
suggestion.rationale: Code-signing cert theft typically follows compromise of CA credentials or HSM access. Pipeline extracted zero credential-access or persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multi-failed authentication attempts against DigiCert HSM/key-storage, successful logins followed by certificate export operations, or cert-signing requests using non-standard APIs or tooling.

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution Using Stolen Code-Signing Certs
suggestion.rationale: The ultimate impact of cert theft is distribution of malware under a trusted signature. Pipeline failed to suggest detection of unsigned→signed binary transitions or unusual publisher trust chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes executing binaries signed with DigiCert certs where: signer organization ≠ expected software vendor, binary hash is unknown/malicious, or cert-signing timestamp is recent (post-compromise).

suggestion.title: HTTP Request to FortiSandbox with Command Injection Syntax
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' enable exploitation. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being the primary attack vector — unauthenticated POST/GET payloads containing shell metacharacters, command substitution ($()), or backticks targeting FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unauthenticated HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/web interface endpoints containing shell metacharacters or command substitution patterns (e.g., $(id), `whoami`, ; bash). Baseline benign administrative requests and flag outliers with payloads matching command injection regex patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access Attempts to FortiSandbox Web Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker is 'unauthenticated' — this is the access path. Pipeline missed detection of missing or invalid authentication tokens reaching FortiSandbox endpoints, which is the prerequisite for exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP 200/successful responses to restricted endpoints without valid session tokens or authentication headers. Track successful unauthenticated access followed by POST requests within same session.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows 'execute unauthorized commands' — post-exploitation detection. Pipeline generated no execution-phase UCs despite the outcome being documented command execution via OS interpreter.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts (typically root or 'forti*' user) with suspicious command-line arguments (e.g., bash -c, /bin/sh, curl, wget). Establish baseline of legitimate administrative maintenance tasks and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox API Exploitation Attempt Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes HTTP request-based exploitation pathway not captured by pipeline's empty kill chain. Should detect the specific exploitation sequence: discovery → unauthenticated request → injection payload → response anomaly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track three-phase HTTP exploitation signature: (1) unauthenticated request to /api or /admin endpoints → (2) HTTP 200-299 response → (3) subsequent POST/GET with shell metacharacters within 10 seconds. Flag as exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Scanner/Vulnerability Assessment Traffic to FortiSandbox Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' but pipeline generated no UCs for identifying exposed FortiSandbox instances. Should detect port-scanning and vulnerability-scanner probing of typical ports (8080, 8443, 8899).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify inbound connections to FortiSandbox ports (8080/tcp, 8443/tcp, 8899/tcp) from external networks or untrusted internal ranges. Correlate with vulnerability scanner signatures and HTTP User-Agent strings known to probe FortiSandbox.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Proof-of-Concept Command Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Exploits typically validate execution with diagnostic commands. Article's 'unauthorized commands' implies PoC validation traffic. Pipeline should hunt for stereotypical post-exploitation indicators (whoami, id, uname -a output in logs).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiSandbox process logs and syslog for execution of benign diagnostic commands in suspicious context: /usr/bin/id, /usr/bin/whoami, /bin/uname called as children of FortiSandbox service. These are PoC indicators following successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' This is the initial-access vector (T1190) and requires asset-exposure baseline + anomaly detection on exposed FortiSandbox web interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API/management endpoints from unauthenticated sessions or external sources. Alert on 401→200 state transitions, requests containing shell metacharacters in URL/POST parameters, or abnormal request rates to known-vulnerable paths. Cross-reference against asset inventory to flag externally-routable instances due for patching by 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'execute unauthorized commands'—requires payload detection in HTTP streams for command-execution signatures (T1059.001).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Screen HTTP requests targeting FortiSandbox for shell metacharacters, command keywords (bash, cmd, powershell), and injection syntax (`|`, `;`, `$()`, backticks, `&&`, `||`) in parameters. Correlate successful 200 responses with unexpected child-process creation events from FortiSandbox service context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Command injection requires process execution; article implies FortiSandbox service executes arbitrary OS commands. Need process-tree monitoring for abnormal children of the FortiSandbox daemon (T1059).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service/agent with unusual executables (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, nc, curl), command-line obfuscation, or no corresponding HTTP API log entry. Baseline normal FortiSandbox child processes (scanner tools, sandbox analysis) to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-07-19 implies urgent inventory/patch-status validation. Standard vulnerability-scanner + asset-inventory query for unpatched instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-25089 detections; cross-reference against CMDB patch status to identify unpatched or missing-scan instances. Prioritize externally-accessible assets. Alert on any new scanner detections within 48 hours of article publication (7-day lookback).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Lateral Movement via Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article does not restrict scope to single-system impact; successful command injection on network-connected FortiSandbox may enable attacker-orchestrated lateral movement or reconnaissance (T1016, T1018).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation baseline: after successful command-injection detection, monitor spawned processes for network reconnaissance (ipconfig, route, arp, nslookup, ping) or lateral-movement tools (psexec, winrm, ssh). Flag process network-connection events originating from FortiSandbox service context to unusual internal IPs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Asset Exposure & Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and states CISA KEV items are 'currently being exploited.' CVE-2026-25089 is the primary IOC but pipeline extracted nothing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and CMDB for FortiSandbox (all three variants: base, Cloud, PaaS) instances matching CVE-2026-25089. Flag any unpatched assets discovered before federal deadline 2026-07-19. Cross-reference with external exposure checks (Shodan, SSL certificate enumeration) to identify internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Suspicious HTTP Request Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation occurs via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' from 'unauthenticated attacker.' This is the exploitation vector that must be detected at the network/web layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to known FortiSandbox instances for requests containing command injection syntax (backticks, $(), |, &&, ;, etc.) in URI query strings or POST parameters. Correlate unauthenticated source IPs with exploitation attempts. Alert on status 200/500 responses following suspicious payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Command Execution on FortiSandbox Appliances
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability that allows...execute unauthorized commands.' Detection must occur at the process/execution level on compromised appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances, detect process creation or shell command execution spawned from the web service daemon (httpd/nginx user context) without legitimate administrative action. Look for system commands, shell invocation, or privilege escalation attempts originating from the web layer.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Product Inventory & Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes three product variants (FortiSandbox, Cloud, PaaS) all vulnerable. Inventory and patch status tracking is foundational risk management; federal due-date deadline drives urgency.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain real-time inventory of all Fortinet FortiSandbox deployments across variants. Track patch status and compare against CVE-2026-25089 patch version. Generate daily compliance report showing % of environment patched, days remaining before federal deadline, and critical/high-risk unpatched instances requiring immediate action.

suggestion.title: External Exposure Detection for FortiSandbox Web Services
suggestion.rationale: Article's MITRE T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) and 'unauthenticated attacker' context indicate internet exposure is a prerequisite for exploitation. Network-level exposure detection is critical.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect listening HTTP/HTTPS services on Fortinet FortiSandbox appliances via continuous network scanning. Identify which instances are externally reachable (public IP, no WAF, no geographic restrictions). Flag any internet-exposed FortiSandbox that should be internal-only, and correlate with recent inbound connection attempts from external sources.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Security Patch Deployment Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Federal compliance deadline is 2026-07-19 for CVE-2026-25089. Deployment monitoring ensures patches are applied before deadline and validates remediation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Fortinet FortiSandbox patch deployment in real-time. Alert on patch deployment failures, rollbacks, or instances that reject patches. Generate compliance dashboard showing patch deployment timeline vs federal deadline. Flag any instances still running vulnerable versions after deadline expires.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox public-facing exposure detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' can exploit via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' and references 'asset-exposure' template. Core hunt is identifying exposed FortiSandbox instances on public IPs/ASNs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Fortinet FortiSandbox instances (FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS product names) exposed to untrusted networks via port scanning, banner grabbing, or vulnerability scanning. Cross-reference with patch status for CVE-2026-25089.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP command injection payload detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' deliver the OS command injection. Need to detect obfuscated command sequences in HTTP POST/GET parameters to FortiSandbox endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP traffic to FortiSandbox instances for payloads containing command substitution syntax (backticks, $(), |, ;, &&) or common OS injection patterns (sh -c, cmd /c, powershell -enc). Correlate with 401/403 errors to isolate unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation process execution from FortiSandbox parent
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute unauthorized commands' via injection. Once exploited, FortiSandbox process (fortisandbox.exe or daemon) will spawn child processes (bash, sh, powershell, cmd) — monitor for unexpected child processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious child processes spawned by Fortinet FortiSandbox processes (typically running as root/SYSTEM). Expected children: none or only internal Fortinet binaries. Flag: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh as children of FortiSandbox parent.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated API access to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' can reach endpoints. Baseline should detect missing or bypassed authentication to FortiSandbox administrative API endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox API endpoints (e.g., /api/*, /admin/*, /upload/) that return 200/201 success codes WITHOUT prior authentication tokens or with default credentials. Baseline expected: all API calls must include valid session/bearer tokens.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox vulnerability scanner detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates remediation check. Pipeline should detect failed patch scans or vulnerability scanner hits for CVE-2026-25089 on Fortinet products.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with asset inventory to identify Fortinet FortiSandbox instances (all variants) with unpatched status for CVE-2026-25089. Flag any scan finding with severity CRIT dated after 2026-07-19 (federal patch due date).

suggestion.title: Command injection obfuscation in FortiSandbox HTTP logs
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'specifically crafted' requests. Attackers often obfuscate payloads with URL encoding, hex encoding, or variable expansion. Need to detect decoded/normalized injection attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Decode URL-encoded, hex-encoded, and variable-expanded HTTP request bodies targeting FortiSandbox. Normalize and check for OS command metacharacters (|, ;, &, `, $, newlines) in parameters. Alert on any match to unauthenticated endpoints.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline omitted detection for the exploitation vector itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection patterns: shell metacharacters (;|&), path traversal, base64-encoded payloads, or unusually long parameters targeting known vulnerable paths. Alert on unauthenticated requests matching these patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability 'allows execution of unauthorized commands.' Pipeline did not create UC for post-injection process creation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected processes spawned by FortiSandbox service accounts. Flag reverse shells, command-line tools (curl, wget, powershell), and scripts originating from FortiSandbox working directories or parent processes.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation implies active wild exploitation and T1190 requires public-facing asset. Article does not specify scope; must verify exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Flag any with internet-routable IPs, inbound internet firewall rules, or public DNS resolution. Cross-check patch status against federal due-date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Native Log Exploitation Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Fortinet vendor — native logs would contain HTTP errors, authorization failures, and command execution events. Pipeline suggested standard asset-exposure template but no product-specific analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox audit/application logs for HTTP request anomalies, 'unauthorized action' events, failed sandbox operations, or command execution records. Correlate with external web-access logs to confirm two-way signal.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-25089 affects Fortinet FortiSandbox products. Standard asset-exposure baseline—any scanner hit against vulnerable endpoint should trigger.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detecting CVE-2026-25089 against FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, or FortiSandbox PaaS endpoints. Include patch status; patches deployed after federal due date (2026-07-19) indicate delayed remediation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox Management Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' exploits via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'—baseline legitimate auth patterns, then alert on repeated unauthenticated access spikes or known-bad payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of authenticated vs unauthenticated HTTP traffic to FortiSandbox web interface. Alert on spike in HTTP 401/403 responses to appliance from single source; correlate with POST/PUT requests bearing binary or special characters typical of command injection payloads.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution on FortiSandbox Host Post-HTTP Request
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection'—successful exploitation spawns processes. Look for unexpected child processes on FortiSandbox appliance correlated with unauthenticated HTTP requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox endpoint logs for process spawning (bash, sh, cmd) from web server processes (nginx, httpd) or management daemon running under non-standard user. Alert if spawning process does not match hardened baseline (e.g., legitimate update/health-check scripts only).

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Anomaly to FortiSandbox Cloud/PaaS Ingestion Points
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS variants—these are cloud-hosted; successful exploitation may leave API/HTTP audit trail. Monitor for malformed or overly large request bodies targeting known injection-prone endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/PUT requests to FortiSandbox Cloud API endpoints with body size ≥2KB or encoding anomalies (multiple null bytes, escaped shell metacharacters). Correlate with geographic source mismatches or after-hours access patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Update/Patch Status Regression
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date is 2026-07-19. Post-deadline, any system still vulnerable is a compliance violation and active-exploitation risk; SOC should track version/patch applied date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline: all FortiSandbox endpoints report patched version post-2026-07-19. Weekly audit report of any endpoint still running unpatched version; escalate if patch was available >7 days prior. Correlate with exploitation attempt logs.

suggestion.title: HTTP exploitation attempts against FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — requires monitoring for POST/GET patterns and payload inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (typical ports 8080, 443, 8443) containing shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or OS command prefixes (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, powershell). Correlate with failed authentication or absence of valid API tokens.

suggestion.title: Unexpected process execution from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: OS command injection vulnerability implies injected commands execute in FortiSandbox process context. Article: 'execute unauthorized commands' — requires process-level telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process spawning (cmd.exe, sh, bash, powershell) with parent process=FortiSandbox service or fnsandbox.exe. Baseline legitimate sandbox activity and flag anomalies, especially those preceded by HTTP 200 responses or unusual network inbound traffic.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox application errors and exploitation signatures
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts (even failed ones) generate logs. Article: CVE is in active use, federal due date 2026-07-19 — implies high attack volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FortiSandbox logs for HTTP 400/403/500 responses clustered around OS command keywords (pipe, semicolon, backtick, $(), etc.) or suspicious URI path traversal (/../../). Cross-reference log timestamps with network IDS alerts for the same source IP.

suggestion.title: Network reconnaissance of FortiSandbox infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV article emphasizes federal asset inventory. Attack precedes exploitation — reconnaissance of exposed FortiSandbox instances is prerequisite.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track DNS queries for FortiSandbox-related domains and cloud variants (forticloud.fortinet.com). Flag external sources probing typical FortiSandbox API endpoints (/api/v2, /admin, /cgi-bin). Correlate with subsequent HTTP POST attempts.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Cloud and PaaS exploitation variants
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names three deployment modes: on-prem, Cloud, PaaS. Each has different network signatures. Single hunt insufficient.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Cloud/PaaS variants, monitor API authentication failures and successful POSTs to sandbox submission endpoints preceded by unauthenticated requests. Check cloud audit logs (Fortinet Cloud API logs) for anomalous command execution or file staging.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 presence in vulnerability scans
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV due date 2026-07-19 creates audit baseline. Detection of unpatched systems is prerequisite for incident response and forensics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any FortiSandbox instance (all versions pre-patch) visible in network scanner results as unpatched for CVE-2026-25089. Cross-reference with firewall rules permitting inbound HTTP(S) from untrusted networks. Use as hunt lead for post-compromise forensics.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated attacker' exploitation — implies exposed instances on internet-facing infrastructure. Text: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS assets via network scanning or asset management system. Alert on any internet-routable access to standard FortiSandbox ports (443, 8000+). Cross-reference against approved external-facing systems.
