suggestion.title: HTTP Injection Payload Detection — CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: Core exploitation mechanism: 'OS command injection vulnerability' via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests'. Detection must monitor payload inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), newlines) in query strings or POST bodies targeting FortiSandbox endpoints. Known payloads for CVE-2026-25089 should be extracted from PoC or vendor advisory and added to WAF/NGFW rules.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker gains ability to 'execute unauthorized commands' post-injection. Detection required to catch shell spawning from compromised sandbox process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by FortiSandbox services (fortisandbox.exe, sandbox runner, etc.). Alert on unexpected commands, reverse shells, reconnaissance utilities, or network I/O. Baseline normal sandbox behavior and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox CVE-2026-25089 Patch Compliance Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article sets federal due date 2026-07-19 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'. Compliance scanning essential for asset inventory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for all FortiSandbox instances. Filter by CVE-2026-25089 and patch status. Flag any unpatched or unscanned instances; escalate per organizational SLA relative to federal due date (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: Fortinet Suspicious HTTP Error Rates
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated injection attacks would generate malformed requests; monitoring abnormal HTTP error codes to FortiSandbox endpoints detects reconnaissance and exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTP 4xx/5xx response rates for FortiSandbox endpoints. Alert on sustained spikes in 400, 403, 500, 502 responses, particularly with identical User-Agent strings or originating from single IP. Correlate with malformed payloads in access logs.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-25089 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline must generate scanner-matched detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect vulnerability scanner alerts or findings matching CVE-2026-25089 against Fortinet FortiSandbox hosts. Alert on confirmed vulnerable versions (pre-2026-07-19 patch date) to identify assets requiring immediate remediation per CISA KEV federal due date.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox HTTP Command Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Requires HTTP-level detection rule for malicious request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints for command injection payloads (shell metacharacters, backticks, $(), semicolons in parameter values). Correlate with unauthenticated session identifiers. Flag requests to known-vulnerable endpoints within 72 hours of patch release (2026-07-19).

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'execute unauthorized commands.' Process-level detection required for post-exploitation command execution spawned from sandbox processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawning from FortiSandbox service accounts (fortinet, forti_sandbox, etc.) with unusual command lines (cmd.exe, bash, powershell, curl, wget). Baseline expected maintenance processes and alert on anomalies within 48 hours of CVE publication or patch deployment.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Fortinet FortiSandbox Public IP Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references T1190 (public-facing application) and warns 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Asset discovery rule required to identify exposed FortiSandbox instances on external IPs/ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Fortinet FortiSandbox instances with public IP assignment or external access routes. Cross-reference with firewall rules permitting inbound HTTP/HTTPS to FortiSandbox service ports. Flag any instances lacking recent patch (post-2026-07-19) as critical for immediate isolation/patching per CISA KEV mandate.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Authentication Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker.' Detection rule required for authentication bypass or missing credential validation in FortiSandbox HTTP handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox access logs for HTTP requests to sensitive endpoints (upload, execute, admin, API) without valid session/auth tokens. Alert on 403/401 responses followed by successful 200 responses from same source (auth bypass attempt). Correlate with IDS/IPS alerts for command injection signatures.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: FortiSandbox Detected on Internet-Facing Interface
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation by 'unauthenticated attacker' via HTTP requests against public-facing instances. CISA KEV status indicates active exploitation in the wild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for FortiSandbox instances exposed on internet-routable networks using port-scanning telemetry, passive DNS, and certificate enumeration. Correlate with vulnerability scanner inventory to identify systems claiming patch-status against actual product version. Alert on instances where patch due-date (2026-07-19) has passed without remediation.

suggestion.title: HTTP Command Injection Payload Detection to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is exploited 'via specifically crafted HTTP requests' using 'OS command injection' delivery mechanism. Detection must target HTTP request content.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for requests to FortiSandbox endpoints containing command-injection payloads: shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, `, $(), backticks), script-execution syntax (sh -c, bash -c, powershell -command), or environment-variable expansion patterns. Establish baseline of normal request patterns and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution on FortiSandbox via Command Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'execute unauthorized commands' after injection. Process-execution logs on target system should be monitored for post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process creation on FortiSandbox systems, particularly shell spawns or scripting-interpreter execution (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) that originate from HTTP service contexts or lack corresponding authenticated user sessions. Baseline normal process execution and detect anomalies.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Verification for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV mandates federal patch by 2026-07-19. Pipeline's own guidance notes patch-lag risk: 'worth one quick check across fleet' even if scanners report patched status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-validate patch status reported by vulnerability scanners against actual product version data from EDR/CMDB. Flag instances with claimed-patched status that cannot be verified by telemetry, or where patch deployment lags >7 days post-announcement.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Product Version Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Multiple product variants affected ('FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS'). Attacker must enumerate variant before exploitation; reconnaissance precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints likely to expose version information (/api/version, /status, /about, root-path enumeration). Alert on repeated version-probing requests from same source IP, particularly if followed within hours by exploitation-pattern requests.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Lateral Movement from FortiSandbox Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Command-execution capability post-compromise provides foothold for internal pivot. OS-command-injection context enables downstream lateral-movement attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After command-injection exploitation patterns are detected, monitor FortiSandbox system for outbound lateral-movement indicators: credential-access attempts (lsass.exe, hashes dumped), network scanning, remote-administration tool downloads, or reverse-shell connections to internal systems. Alert on lateral-movement tool execution in FortiSandbox service context.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Internet-Facing FortiSandbox Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker' and CISA KEV implies active exploitation of 'public-facing' systems. No hunt for exposed FortiSandbox instances (listening on 443, 8080, or typical mgmt ports) was generated despite this being the canonical first step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Fortinet FortiSandbox instances accessible from untrusted networks (public IP ranges). Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-25089 patch status. Alert on any unpatched instances still listening externally; prioritize by exposure date and traffic volume.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Exploitation Attempt Detection (FortiSandbox)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' exploited via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' No use case captures payload pattern matching for injection attempts (e.g., backticks, $(), semicolons, pipes in HTTP params).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for shell metacharacters (backtick, $(), |, ;, &&, ||) in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate with failed command injection signatures (403/500 responses suggesting blocked payloads). Alert on successful exploitation indicators: process spawning from FortiSandbox service with elevated privileges or unusual child processes (bash, sh, cmd).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Process Execution from FortiSandbox Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker ability to 'execute unauthorized commands'—this is the post-exploitation execution phase. No detection for anomalous process spawning from the FortiSandbox service context was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal child processes spawned by FortiSandbox service (typically none or only legitimate maintenance tasks). Alert on unexpected process spawning: shells (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell), net/curl/wget (data exfil), cron/at (persistence). Severity escalates if spawned process attempts network communication or file access outside expected FortiSandbox data directories.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Version Inventory & Patch Compliance (CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article names affected products ('FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS') and federal due date 2026-07-19. Pipeline generated zero scanner/inventory hunts despite CISA mandate requiring remediation tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable) for CVE-2026-25089 findings. Cross-reference against FortiSandbox inventory (version, deployment type: on-prem/Cloud/PaaS). Generate daily compliance report: count unpatched instances, oldest patch lag, internet-facing exposure status. Flag any instance unpatched 48 hours before federal due date (2026-07-17) as escalation candidate.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Application Log Analysis for Injection Failures
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific exploitation vector but pipeline did not surface log analysis use case. FortiSandbox application logs should contain HTTP request context, parameter inspection, and execution flow traces useful for post-compromise analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Review FortiSandbox application logs for requests containing injection-like syntax (%, ${}, `, semicolons in parameters). Correlate log timestamp with firewall/IDS alerts on same source IP. Pivot on successful exploitation: look for follow-up requests (data collection, lateral movement probes) from attacker IP within 5 minutes of injection.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — direct indicator of initial-access exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to FortiSandbox (any variant) endpoints that lack valid authentication tokens or session cookies, especially POSTs with HTTP status 2xx responses after previously failing auth attempts. Baseline legitimate access patterns and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection in HTTP Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' and 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — signature-level detection for shell metacharacters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell metacharacters (pipe |, backticks `, semicolon ;, &&, ||, $(), command substitution) in HTTP request parameters sent to FortiSandbox. Particularly focus on POST bodies and query strings that reach application endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and substitute CVE-2026-25089 — critical for identifying unpatched instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-25089 matches. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify FortiSandbox instances (Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, FortiSandbox PaaS) and filter by patch status. Flag unpatched instances due 2026-07-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'execute unauthorized commands' — detection of actual command execution via process monitoring tied to web service compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from FortiSandbox service accounts (typically unprivileged). Correlate timing of suspicious HTTP requests (from detection 2) with child process creation from the web service parent. Look for cmd.exe, bash, or shell interpreters launched by the Fortinet process.

suggestion.title: Multi-Variant FortiSandbox Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three vulnerable products: 'FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS' — cloud and on-prem variants require different discovery methods.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset discovery hunt for all three FortiSandbox variants — query cloud infrastructure logs for FortiSandbox Cloud/PaaS instances, network scans for on-prem deployments, and SSL/TLS certificate logs for exposed endpoints. Correlate against vulnerability scanner to find unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: HTTP POST with Injection Payloads to Fortinet Services
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector as 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — behavioral detection for known payload patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST requests to Fortinet services with common command injection payloads: encoded pipes/semicolons, command substitution syntax $(), backticks, shell environment variables ($PATH, $HOME), or base64-encoded shell commands in request bodies.

suggestion.title: DIRAC FileCatalog database query timing spikes and anomalous result counts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'passes the result to eval' implying unusual result set sizes or timing patterns precede RCE. SQL injection typically causes observable query performance degradation or result set anomalies. Not covered by existing UCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DIRAC FileCatalog/DatasetManager query latency and result-set cardinality. SQL injection attacks often exhibit: (1) sudden increase in query execution time for checkDataset, (2) result sets orders of magnitude larger than baseline, (3) UNION/subquery patterns in slow queries. Baseline by authenticated user and dataset size.

suggestion.title: Python eval() or exec() bytecode compilation detection (post-RCE persistence)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'passes result to eval' but no UC directly detects eval() calls or dynamically-compiled Python bytecode. This is the execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for signs of eval/exec in DIRAC Python logs: (1) ProcessMemory containing __pycache__ or compiled Python code generated from non-standard sources, (2) DIRAC spawning Python with unusual arguments like -c or piped stdin, (3) Python processes with parent=FileCatalog but unusual interpreter arguments.

suggestion.title: ProxyDB or token credential file access post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'ProxyDB' and 'token store' in UC_102_4 searches but provides no standalone hunt for theft of proxy credentials, which are high-value in grid computing environments. Mentioned in UC_102_4 but deserves separate high-confidence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized read/copy of DIRAC proxy certificates and tokens: (1) process with parent=python/FileCatalog reading /opt/dirac/*/ProxyDB* or ~/.dirac/proxy* or similar, (2) ProxyDB files copied to /tmp or world-writable locations, (3) base64 encoding of ProxyDB immediately after access (staging for exfil).

suggestion.title: DIRAC service restart or abnormal termination post-RCE (incident recovery signal)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes critical RCE vulnerability but does not mention detection of defensive response (service restart/kill). Administrators detecting compromise often restart services; absence of restart may indicate adversary maintaining persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DIRAC service process termination with: (1) prior shell spawning from Python parent, (2) credential file access, or (3) network exfiltration. Sudden kill -9 or service stop immediately following RCE indicators suggest incident response. Conversely, ABSENCE of restart after RCE indicators suggests persistence.

suggestion.title: Dataset parameter validation bypass or DIRAC API schema evasion
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'checkDataset function passes its datasets argument directly to the backend DB handler' — no UC validates that datasets parameter is being properly sanitized or schema-enforced. Input validation failures are the root cause.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for checkDataset calls with datasets parameter containing: (1) data types not matching expected schema (strings where int expected), (2) length anomalies (>10KB for normally <100B parameter), (3) special characters like quotes/semicolons in datasets value before reaching database handler, (4) charset encoding anomalies (UTF-16, double-encoding).

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — pipeline generated zero detection for this initial access vector. Need to hunt for HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Fortinet FortiSandbox endpoints (ports 8443, 8080 or known FortiSandbox service URIs) originating from external/untrusted sources. Flag requests with anomalous headers, injected command syntax, or patterns matching known exploitation PoCs for CVE-2026-25089.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Process
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'OS command injection vulnerability' but pipeline captured no execution-layer detection. Need process-tree telemetry from the affected sandboxing application itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child process creation under FortiSandbox parent processes (typical parents: fortisandboxd, httpd, or FortiSandbox service account) with suspicious command lines (cmd.exe, bash, curl, wget, or reverse-shell indicators). Baseline legitimate child processes and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Startup Without Patch Evidence
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'Federal patch due: 2026-07-19' and that 'patch lag is the silent killer' — pipeline should detect unpatched instances still running post-deadline. Asset exposure hunt requires version detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for FortiSandbox/FortiSandbox Cloud/FortiSandbox PaaS instances running versions ≤ the patch-fix version for CVE-2026-25089. Cross-reference against scan dates and boot timestamps; flag instances with no evidence of patch application after 2026-07-19 deadline.

suggestion.title: HTTP Request Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability is triggered by 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' but no payload-level detection was generated. Network-based sensors can catch the actual exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Deploy IDS/WAF signatures for CVE-2026-25089 exploitation patterns. Look for HTTP requests containing shell metacharacters (;, |, &, $(), backticks), command-substitution syntax, or known PoC payload signatures targeting FortiSandbox endpoint paths.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'. This is the primary delivery mechanism and should be the first detection layer. Pipeline omitted HTTP-level indicators entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/HTTPS traffic to FortiSandbox management interfaces (typical ports: 80, 443, 8080, 8443, 18443) for requests from external/untrusted sources. Baseline legitimate admin requests and alert on anomalous payloads, oversized request bodies, or request patterns deviating from normal operational traffic. Correlate external IP probing multiple FortiSandbox instances.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Child Process Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'execute unauthorized commands' directly establishes execution phase. Pipeline generated zero process-level detections despite this being the consequence of successful HTTP injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service accounts or parent processes. Baseline legitimate process trees for each FortiSandbox version and detect deviations: shell interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell), script engines, or system utilities (curl, wget, nc) spawned from HTTP-handling contexts. Inspect command lines for shell metacharacters indicating injection payloads.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerability class as 'OS command injection'. HTTP payloads will contain injection syntax. Pipeline omitted syntax-level detection for backticks, command substitution, pipes, and separators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect HTTP request payloads (URL parameters, POST bodies, headers) to FortiSandbox endpoints for OS command injection metacharacters: backticks (`), dollar-parenthesis `$()`, semicolons (`;`), pipes (`|`), logical operators (`&&`, `||`), newlines. Flag chained commands (e.g., `cmd1; cmd2`, `cmd1 | cmd2`) and base64/URL-encoded variants thereof. Tuning: exclude vendor telemetry and legitimate admin scripts.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Vulnerability Scanner Detection Cross-Reference
suggestion.rationale: Article references template-based asset-exposure hunt pattern. Must correlate scanner results (Nessus, Rapid7, Qualys) against patch status before federal deadline 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners for CVE-2026-25089 detections. Cross-reference flagged FortiSandbox instances against patch management system to identify claimed-patched vs. actually-patched hosts (patch lag). Alert on any unpatched instances in production. Prioritize instances internet-facing or reachable from external networks given unauthenticated exploitation vector.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Error Spike and Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation attempts often leave HTTP error artifacts (400/500 errors) in application/access logs prior to RCE. Article describes 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' — malformed payloads may error before breakthrough.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid sequences of HTTP 400/401/403/500 errors to FortiSandbox endpoints from the same source IP with subsequent successful request (200) or process execution. Monitor application logs for exception traces or permission-denied events preceding unauthorized command execution. Alert on error-then-silence-then-execution patterns typical of automated exploitation.

suggestion.title: External Network Reconnaissance to FortiSandbox Service Ports
suggestion.rationale: Pre-exploitation reconnaissance is standard workflow. Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated' implying attackers must first locate exposed instances. Pipeline omitted network discovery indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on port scans or connection attempts to known FortiSandbox service ports (8080, 8443, 443, 18443) from external IPs. Flag scanning patterns targeting multiple internal FortiSandbox instances within short time windows. Correlate scan activity with subsequent exploitation attempts (HTTP payloads) from the same source to confirm attack progression.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox with Injection Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' — pipeline generated zero use cases despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox endpoints lacking authentication headers or credentials, combined with suspicious payloads (shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax). Correlate with 4xx/5xx responses (failed injection attempts) or unusual response sizes (successful execution output).

suggestion.title: Detect OS Command Injection Patterns in HTTP Request Bodies
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' — no use case for detecting injection patterns themselves, only asset exposure template mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP request payloads containing shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, &&, ||) sent to FortiSandbox listening ports, especially when combined with command keywords (id, whoami, cat, curl, wget, nc).

suggestion.title: Monitor FortiSandbox Process Execution for Unexpected Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation would spawn OS commands — article states 'execute unauthorized commands' but pipeline omitted post-exploitation monitoring use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline FortiSandbox process behavior (fortisandbox service, daemon processes). Alert on unexpected child process spawning (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) or abnormal parent-child relationships originating from FortiSandbox listening ports.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Inventory Check
suggestion.rationale: Article implies public-facing FortiSandbox instances are vulnerable to unauthenticated exploitation — asset inventory is a prerequisite for targeted hunting but was buried in template reference rather than as explicit use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for all FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify which instances are reachable from untrusted networks. Prioritize instances running unpatched versions against CVE-2026-25089 (pre-2026-07-19 remediation timeline).

suggestion.title: Detect Successful Remote Command Execution via Exit Code / Output Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline generated no post-exploitation indicators — successful exploitation would show attackers retrieving command output or establishing interactive shells via HTTP responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for HTTP responses from FortiSandbox containing shell command output (permission denied, no such file, bash prompts) or base64-encoded payloads. Correlate large response sizes following suspicious HTTP requests with known command execution output patterns.

suggestion.title: Timeline Correlation: FortiSandbox Scanning + Exploitation Attempts Before Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV due date is 2026-07-19 (3 days from article publish); pipeline missed urgency-driven hunting combining recon + exploitation attempts in same timeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate port scanning activity (Shodan-style reconnaissance) against FortiSandbox listener ports with follow-up HTTP injection attempts from same source IP within hours/days. Pre-patch vulnerability window (now through 2026-07-19) represents highest risk period.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Pipeline generated no detection for the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox instances for injection-attempt signatures: shell metacharacters (backticks, $(), |, ;), encoded payloads, or command-substitution patterns. Flag requests from untrusted IPs given CISA KEV active-exploitation status.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Unauthorized OS Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'OS command injection vulnerability allows...execute unauthorized commands.' Must detect post-exploitation child processes and abnormal activity from FortiSandbox service accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by the FortiSandbox daemon (sandboxd/fortisandbox user context), particularly shells, script interpreters, or outbound network connections from the sandbox process tree.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Asset Exposure Inventory Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application' exploited in the wild. Prerequisite hunt: identify all exposed FortiSandbox/Cloud/PaaS instances before exploitation occurs; federal patch deadline is 2026-07-19.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances reachable from the internet or high-risk network segments. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-25089 vulnerability data to flag all running vulnerable versions as critical priority.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Error Spike & Malformed Request Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Failed exploitation attempts will leave audit/error log traces. Pipeline surfaced no detection for pre-exploitation reconnaissance or failed attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate spikes in HTTP 5xx responses, input-validation exceptions, or shell-execution errors on FortiSandbox endpoints with source IPs. Alert on repeated exploitation attempts from a single source within 1 hour, indicating active scanning or campaign.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox API Command Injection Payload Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—no detection for malicious HTTP payloads targeting FortiSandbox API was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Fortinet FortiSandbox API endpoints for command injection metacharacters (backticks, $(), pipes, semicolons, shell redirects) in query parameters, headers, or request bodies. Alert on unauthenticated requests containing these patterns.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Suspicious Child Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability allows execution of 'unauthorized commands'—no detection for abnormal process trees spawned from FortiSandbox service processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on FortiSandbox core processes (fssandbox, fssandbox-api, etc.) spawning children with shell interpreters (bash, cmd.exe, PowerShell) or suspicious command-line arguments. Baseline benign process trees and flag deviations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Unpatched Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS as affected with federal patch deadline 2026-07-19—no asset-inventory or vulnerability-scanner query was generated to locate vulnerable instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for Fortinet FortiSandbox instances (all variants) with patch status ≤ 2026-07-18. Cross-reference network exposure scans to identify internet-facing instances. Alert on unpatched or externally-accessible assets.

suggestion.title: HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox Unauthenticated Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is triggered via 'unauthenticated attacker' access—no detection for attempted auth bypass or requests to endpoints that should require credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox API endpoints for requests lacking valid authentication tokens or credentials. Establish baseline of legitimate auth patterns and flag deviations, especially from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox public-facing asset exposure scan
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Exploitation requires network-reachable FortiSandbox instance; asset inventory is mandatory hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Fortinet FortiSandbox, FortiSandbox Cloud, and FortiSandbox PaaS instances accessible to internet-routable networks. Correlate with patch management to identify unpatched versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089 before 2026-07-19 federal deadline.

suggestion.title: HTTP exploitation attempts to FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'via specifically crafted HTTP requests.' Unauthenticated HTTP POST/PUT with command payloads is signature of exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to known FortiSandbox API endpoints containing shell metacharacters (|, ;, &, $(), backticks), base64-encoded command payloads, or command-injection patterns from unauthenticated sessions or default credentials.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized command execution spawned by FortiSandbox process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: 'execute unauthorized commands.' Successful exploitation will manifest as shell (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, /bin/sh, /bin/bash) spawned as child of FortiSandbox service process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation events where parent is FortiSandbox service/Java process spawning command interpreter or shell, particularly with system-level privileges or unusual working directory contexts.

suggestion.title: Known exploit PoC signature detection for CVE-2026-25089
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active wild exploitation. Public exploit code likely exists; IPS/WAF signatures should detect exploit patterns specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor threat intel feeds for published CVE-2026-25089 exploit code; deploy signature-based detection for known PoC exploit patterns; correlate IDS/IPS/WAF alerts tagged with this CVE to identify active exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox patch compliance audit by deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due date 2026-07-19. Any unpatched instance post-deadline represents compliance violation and breach risk given CISA KEV active exploitation status.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit Fortinet FortiSandbox (all variants: on-prem, Cloud, PaaS) for CVE-2026-25089 patch status. Generate compliance report pre- and post-2026-07-19. Flag unpatched instances as critical remediation priority with escalation path to federal compliance officer if applicable.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Exposed Instance Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and identifies vulnerability in 'public-facing application' — first defensive step is locating exposed FortiSandbox instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for FortiSandbox (any version) with internet-facing ports exposed. Cross-reference external IP scanners, shodan, and CDR logs for public accessibility. Prioritize instances matching vulnerable product line.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Requests to FortiSandbox APIs
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack via 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' to 'unauthenticated attacker' — authentication bypass is the entry vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox web access logs for HTTP requests that succeed without valid authentication tokens (missing/invalid auth headers, no session cookie). Flag requests to known-vulnerable API endpoints (e.g. /api/*, /admin/*) from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: OS Command Injection Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack vector: 'OS command injection vulnerability that allows execution of unauthorized commands' — successful exploitation manifests as unexpected child processes from FortiSandbox service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation where parent = FortiSandbox binary/service (fortisandbox.exe, java FortiSandbox process). Alert on shell spawning (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh), especially with obfuscated or suspicious command-line arguments. Establish baseline of legitimate FortiSandbox child processes.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement After FortiSandbox Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Once OS-level execution is achieved via injected commands, attacker typically escalates and moves laterally — article establishes execution capability but SOC should hunt downstream pivoting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: From compromised FortiSandbox host, hunt for network reconnaissance (arp, net view, nmap), credential dumping (mimikatz, secretsdump), and lateral movement tools (psexec, wmic, ssh to other hosts). Correlate timing with initial HTTP exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance for CVE-2026-25089 by Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch deadline 2026-07-19 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer' — proactive hunt for unpatched vulnerable versions before active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventory for Fortinet FortiSandbox/FortiSandbox Cloud/FortiSandbox PaaS versions confirmed vulnerable to CVE-2026-25089. Cross-check patch deployment records. Alert on any instances still running vulnerable version after deadline date.

suggestion.title: Fortinet Advisory Indicators in Web Access Logs
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as exploitation method — IDS/WAP/WAF rules from Fortinet advisory should detect payload patterns if available.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Check Fortinet security bulletins for CVE-2026-25089 exploitation signatures. Apply WAF/IDS rules to catch malicious HTTP request patterns. Monitor 4xx/5xx error rates from FortiSandbox endpoints as byproduct of fuzzed exploit attempts.

suggestion.title: Notarized Binary Executing Suspicious Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Notarized Dropper' and 'Pass Gatekeeper Checks'—the attack vector is a legitimate-appearing signed binary spawning payload. Pipeline missed detection for bypass of macOS code-signing validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes with valid Apple notarization and code signature (high trust score) spawning child processes with low prevalence or unsigned binaries. Focus on .app bundles executed from Downloads or user-writable paths that then spawn shell interpreters or non-standard binaries.

suggestion.title: CrashStealer Dropper-to-Payload Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'CrashStealer' by name and 'dropper' function. Pipeline failed to recognize multi-stage execution pattern (dropper→payload) inherent to malware delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent-child process relationships where a DMG-mounted or downloaded executable launches secondary binaries via fork/execve. Look for process trees: legitimate binary → /bin/sh → suspicious payload, or direct injection via dylib loading.

suggestion.title: Credential/Data Exfiltration from CrashStealer Activity
suggestion.rationale: Malware is explicitly named 'CrashStealer' (stealer variant), indicating credential/data harvesting. Article topic establishes data theft as primary objective. Pipeline extracted no collection/exfiltration use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or low-reputation processes reading Safari/Chrome credential databases, Keychain queries, or ~/Library/Cookies. Correlate with outbound HTTPS traffic to non-browser C2 domains (TLS cert inspection for anomalous SNI). Look for processes accessing /Library/Preferences or ~/Library with high entropy reads.

suggestion.title: macOS Gatekeeper/Quarantine Attribute Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly calls out 'Pass Gatekeeper Checks'—detection should surface attempts to bypass or remove quarantine flags that Gatekeeper relies on. Pipeline missed defense-evasion specific to macOS security controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes executing xattr commands to strip 'com.apple.quarantine' attributes from downloaded files, or use of SetFile to manipulate creation/modification times. Monitor for dyld environment variable injection (DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES) to bypass notarization checks.

suggestion.title: Launchd Persistence Registration from Notarized Context
suggestion.rationale: Malware leveraging Gatekeeper bypass suggests persistence mechanism. Typical macOS malware installs LaunchAgent/LaunchDaemon. Pipeline failed to anticipate post-execution persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect writes to ~/Library/LaunchAgents or /Library/LaunchDaemons from processes spawned by notarized binaries or code-signed applications. Inspect .plist files for suspicious Program/ProgramArguments pointing to user-writable locations or obfuscated shell commands.

suggestion.title: Suspicious DMG Mount and Execution Sequence
suggestion.rationale: CrashStealer distribution likely via DMG (common macOS delivery). Article's focus on 'dropper' implies archive-based distribution. Pipeline missed initial access detection for disk image mounting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate hdiutil or mount operations (identifying .dmg files) with near-simultaneous execution of binaries from /Volumes/ mount points. Flag when mount is followed by process execution from temporary or user-writable paths, especially if parent is browser or email client.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox HTTP Exploitation Attempts (CVE-2026-25089)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specifically crafted HTTP requests' as attack vector; no detection UC generated despite being the primary initial access method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints for exploitation signatures: unusual HTTP methods, parameter injection attempts, command metacharacters (`;|&$()`) in GET/POST parameters, or large payloads targeting known vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with unauthenticated access (missing auth tokens/headers) and non-200 error responses.

suggestion.title: OS Command Execution from FortiSandbox Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands'; no detection UC for resultant process execution despite this being the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service processes (parent: fortisandbox.exe, fortisandbox-cloud, etc.) with suspicious command lines containing shell invocations (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, powershell.exe) or command metacharacters. Flag processes with system-level privileges spawned unexpectedly.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to FortiSandbox Management Interface
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploitability hinges on unauthenticated attacker capability; article states attacker requires no credentials, yet no UC for authentication-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline authenticated vs. unauthenticated requests to FortiSandbox endpoints. Alert on HTTP requests to FortiSandbox endpoints (e.g., `/admin`, `/api`, `/sandbox`) from external sources with absent, invalid, or expired authentication tokens/cookies. Cross-reference with GeoIP for known-attacker ASNs or Shodan/Censys scan signatures.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Cloud/PaaS Command Injection Payload Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article lists three product variants (FortiSandbox, Cloud, PaaS); no specific detection for cloud-hosted instances or multi-tenant exploitation despite distinct hosting footprints and attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP), monitor FortiSandbox PaaS API calls and HTTP payloads for command injection patterns. Flag requests with shell metacharacters in request bodies, suspicious parameter encoding, or excessively long payloads targeting known-vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with container escape attempts or elevated IAM role assumption.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089 Scanner/Exploitation Tool Signatures
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entries are actively exploited in the wild; no UC for detecting known exploit tooling or mass-scanning activity targeting this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known Metasploit module, POC, or commercial exploit tool signatures in HTTP User-Agent headers, request patterns, or timing. Detect mass-scanning behavior: repeated rapid requests to different FortiSandbox instances across your network with identical payloads or User-Agents. Correlate with threat intelligence feeds for CVE-2026-25089 exploitation tooling.

suggestion.title: WordPress wp2shell RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly labels 'wp2shell' as the vulnerability enabling 'Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code'; pipeline extracted no IOCs or use cases. Title establishes public-facing application exploit scenario.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to WordPress endpoints (wp-admin/admin-ajax.php, wp-includes, wp-content) from unauthenticated sources containing encoded payloads, null bytes, or PHP function calls (eval, system, exec, assert). Flag requests missing valid session cookies or Authorization headers.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Creation in WordPress Writable Directories
suggestion.rationale: Naming 'wp2shell' indicates web-shell persistence mechanism; pipeline did not map to T1505.003 or file-creation detections. RCE results in shell artifacts in wp-content/uploads or plugins.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .php, .phtml, or .phar file creation in wp-content/uploads, wp-content/plugins, or wp-content/themes by w3wp.exe or apache2 processes outside maintenance windows. Correlate with preceding suspicious HTTP POST/PUT requests to WordPress files.

suggestion.title: Command Execution Spawned from Web-Server Process
suggestion.rationale: RCE flaw enables arbitrary code execution; pipeline missed command-execution detection despite article establishing execution capability. Need to detect process spawning chain from web server.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or /bin/bash spawned as child of w3wp.exe, apache2, or nginx with parent chain rooted in svchost or apache parent processes. Monitor for base64-encoded command parameters, encoded payloads, or reverse-shell indicators in process arguments.

suggestion.title: Suspicious POST Requests to WordPress Admin AJAX Handler
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE typically targets wp-admin/admin-ajax.php; pipeline did not surface this endpoint-specific exploitation pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to wp-admin/admin-ajax.php action parameter with non-existent or malicious values (action=wp_shell, action=rce, action=exec) from public IPs. Alert on polyglot payloads (.jpg.php, .gif.php) or PHP serialization objects in request body.

suggestion.title: Rapid File Writes Followed by HTTP Requests in Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation chain: HTTP request → file drop → shell execution. Pipeline failed to generate behavioral detections correlating file I/O with network events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file-creation events in web-root directories (wp-content, uploads) within 60 seconds of HTTP requests from the same source IP. Alert if file permissions are world-readable or executed immediately via subsequent HTTP request.

suggestion.title: Encoded Command Parameters in WordPress HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Web-shell exploitation uses base64/hex encoding to obfuscate payloads; pipeline did not surface encoding-pattern or payload-signature detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP request parameters containing base64-encoded strings, hex-encoded sequences, or gzip-compressed payloads targeting WordPress endpoints. Decode and scan for shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, $()), function names (eval, exec, system, passthru), or reverse-shell signatures.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection via WordPress REST/Query Parameter
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes 'unauthenticated RCE via SQL injection'—the SQLi is the entry vector. Article states the exploit targets WordPress core and is unauthenticated, implying web-facing SQL injection in publicly accessible parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor incoming HTTP requests to WordPress installation paths (/wp-admin, /wp-json, /?p=) for SQLi payloads in GET/POST parameters: UNION-based (keywords: UNION, SELECT, WHERE in encoded form %55, %53), time-delay sleep(X) or BENCHMARK(), error-based (MySQL/PostgreSQL error syntax), stacked queries (semicolon-delimited). Baseline legitimate queries first; alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Shell Process Spawned from Web Server Following SQLi Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates RCE endpoint: SQL injection must execute system commands. Article 'wp2shell' naming suggests direct shell access post-exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child process creation from web server processes (www-data, iis apppool, httpd, nginx). Alert on spawning of interpreters (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, python, perl) or utilities (curl, wget, nc) from web-server parent PIDs immediately following HTTP requests. Correlate timing: SQLi request → process creation within <5s.

suggestion.title: Database Error Leakage in HTTP Response (SQLi Indicator)
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection attempts, especially error-based, generate MySQL/PostgreSQL error messages that may leak in HTTP responses. Article describes a live exploit, so error-based SQLi variants are likely attempted first.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP responses containing database error strings: 'MySQL', 'PostgreSQL', 'ORA-', 'SQL Server', 'Syntax error', 'near line', 'SQL query' in response body or HTTP 500+ status codes paired with SQL keywords in request URL. Cross-reference with request parameters for SQLi signatures.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Query Execution from WordPress Instance
suggestion.rationale: SQLi reaching code execution means database is executing attacker-controlled queries. Article emphasizes WordPress core vulnerability, so queries are executed in DB context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database logs for: UNION-based multi-row SELECTs from information_schema, repeated INTO OUTFILE / LOAD_FILE attempts, CREATE FUNCTION or ALTER FUNCTION commands, EXEC/xp_cmdshell (MSSQL), or SELECT...INTO queries writing to filesystem. Compare against baseline WordPress query patterns (wp_posts, wp_users, wp_options tables only).

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from Web Server Post-SQLi
suggestion.rationale: RCE via SQLi typically results in reverse shell, data exfil, or C2 callback. Article's critical severity and RCE nature suggest post-exploit callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected outbound connections (non-standard ports, non-whitelisted destinations) originating from web-server process IP/PID within 30s of SQLi-pattern detection. Establish baseline for legitimate PHP external calls (CDN, mail SMTP); flag deviations to unusual IPs/ports, especially on high-volume data channels or rare protocols (raw socket, DNS tunneling).

suggestion.title: WordPress Administrative User Creation or Privilege Escalation Post-Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated RCE via SQLi to WordPress database allows direct wp_users table modification. Attacker likely persists via new admin account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor wp_users table for unexpected INSERT/UPDATE rows where user_login is new, user_pass hash changed, or user_registered timestamp is recent but admin meta (wp_capabilities) grants admin role. Correlate with SQLi detection events. Flag if no admin user exists in audit logs prior to database change timestamp.

suggestion.title: Detect Malformed Short TLS ClientHello Packets
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '11-Byte TLS Requests' as attack vector. Pipeline missed this obvious network-layer detection signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for TLS handshake packets significantly smaller than expected (≤11 bytes to ClientHello frame). Flag connections originating from external networks attempting to initiate TLS with malformed or incomplete handshake sequences, particularly to ports 443 and 8443.

suggestion.title: Detect OpenSSL Process Crash and Restart Cycles
suggestion.rationale: Article title states vulnerability 'could freeze server memory'—impact is service degradation. Pipeline missed process-level impact detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated rapid restart cycles of OpenSSL/TLS services (e.g., nginx, Apache, custom TLS daemons). Alert on process exit codes indicating abnormal termination (segfault, out-of-memory) followed by immediate re-spawning within <60s window.

suggestion.title: Detect Abnormal Memory Consumption by TLS Processes
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'freeze server memory' as exploit outcome. No detection use case for memory exhaustion was generated despite explicit article focus.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenSSL-linked processes (sslengine, openssl, TLS libraries) for memory allocation spikes >500MB sustained for <5s during TLS connection attempts. Correlate with network traffic anomalies (short malformed packets) to differentiate from legitimate large-file TLS transfers.

suggestion.title: Detect CVE-Related OpenSSL Version Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article references specific OpenSSL 'HollowByte' flaw but pipeline extracted no CVE ID or version ranges. Version enumeration from banners/responses is a fundamental threat intelligence requirement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline OpenSSL version from TLS ServerHello banners (TLS_GREASE, cipher suite patterns). Alert on external reconnaissance (nmap, sslscan) probing for versions matching known HollowByte-affected ranges; escalate if followed by malformed TLS packets.

suggestion.title: Detect Repeated TLS Handshake Failures to Same Target
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation pattern of sending 11-byte requests implies repeated connection attempts. Pipeline missed behavioral anomaly detection for brute-force-style TLS attack probes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sequences of >50 incomplete/malformed TLS handshakes from same source to same target within 60s window. Prioritize if source is external and handshake failures escalate to process crash events on target.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly references 'Seven Malicious Vite npm Packages'—supply-chain attack vector. Pipeline should detect npm install commands pulling from suspicious or typosquatted package names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install, yarn add, pnpm add commands for package names matching known malicious Vite package variants. Alert on post-install script execution or unexpected child processes spawned during package installation. Correlate with package manager manifests (package.json, lock files) for unexpected dependencies.

suggestion.title: Blockchain API Communication from Development Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Blockchain C2'—unusual command-and-control mechanism. Pipeline should detect outbound calls to blockchain nodes, RPC endpoints, or crypto exchanges from development/build environments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS connections to known blockchain RPC endpoints (Ethereum, Polygon, Solana nodes), cryptocurrency exchange APIs, or blockchain explorers from non-standard processes (node.js, JavaScript engines). Flag DNS queries for blockchain service domains originating from npm postinstall scripts.

suggestion.title: JavaScript Post-Install Script RAT Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'RAT delivery' via npm packages—npm packages execute post-install scripts. Pipeline should detect file write, process spawning, or network connectivity from JavaScript/node.js contexts during package installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child processes spawned from npm/yarn/pnpm with unusual command lines (PowerShell, cmd.exe, curl, wget). Detect file writes to temp or system directories from node.js processes. Alert on network connections from npm postinstall context to non-standard ports or blockchain infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article targets Vite build tool ecosystem with malicious packages—suggests name confusion or registry compromise. Detection should flag installations of packages with suspicious or typosquatted names relative to legitimate Vite ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference installed package names against npm registry metadata. Flag packages with unusual author changes, recent owner transfers, or suspicious version jumps. Alert on package installations where version does not match requested range or when package pulled from non-standard registry mirrors.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated JavaScript C2 Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: RAT payload delivered via npm likely uses obfuscated JavaScript. Detection should identify encoded strings, suspicious Base64/hex decoding, or dynamic code evaluation patterns in node_modules execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval(), Function(), require() with dynamically constructed strings executed from node_modules contexts. Alert on decoding of Base64/hex strings followed by network connectivity. Monitor for suspicious Object prototype pollution or require path manipulation patterns.

suggestion.title: Blockchain Wallet Address Hardcoding in Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Blockchain C2 likely requires hardcoded wallet/address references in RAT code. Pipeline should extract and monitor for known malicious blockchain addresses embedded in source code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan npm package source code and compiled artifacts for hardcoded Ethereum/crypto addresses, blockchain transaction hashes, or RPC endpoint URLs. Correlate extracted addresses against threat intelligence feeds for known C2 infrastructure. Alert if extracted addresses appear in on-chain transaction analysis.

suggestion.title: Kubernetes API Reconnaissance from Untrusted Sources
suggestion.rationale: Article states botnet 'hunts exposed AI services' and 'Kubernetes tokens'—implies probing Kubernetes API endpoints. Distinctive attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connection attempts to Kubernetes API ports (6443, 10250, 10255, 9090) from external IPs, especially patterns consistent with rapid automated scanning. Track DNS queries for k8s infrastructure hostnames (*.cluster.local, kube-apiserver) from non-k8s-designated hosts.

suggestion.title: Cloud Service Credential Exfiltration via CLI Tools
suggestion.rationale: Core threat: 'hunts...for cloud keys and Kubernetes tokens.' Botnet must enumerate and exfiltrate credentials programmatically.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmdline patterns harvesting credentials: env variable dumps (env | grep -i aws|token), reads of ~/.aws/*, ~/.kube/config, or /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token. Alert on child process execution from unexpected services (web apps, containers) accessing credential stores.

suggestion.title: Exposed AI/ML Endpoint Brute-Force Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase 'hunts exposed AI services' indicates automated scanning of cloud-hosted ML/AI endpoints for accessible endpoints lacking authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid sequential HTTP requests to common ML API paths (/v1/models, /api/predict, /metrics, /admin) and high-volume non-200 responses (403/404) from single sources. Correlate with known botnet malware signatures or NadMesh C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Service Account Token Read and Exfiltration from Containers
suggestion.rationale: Specific attack vector: Kubernetes tokens stored in predictable container mount point /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/. Article explicitly mentions this threat class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process reads of /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/token or /var/run/secrets/.../.dockercfg from non-system processes. Detect subsequent egress of token-sized data (base64-encoded ~500+ bytes) to external destinations outside cluster network.

suggestion.title: Multi-Cloud Credential Harvesting Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Botnet scanning for credentials across infrastructure implies attempting multiple cloud provider CLI tools and environment variable patterns sequentially from same source.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate rapid attempts to locate AWS (aws-vault, ~/.aws), GCP (gcloud config), and Azure (az login) credential materials from single host. Detect patterns of env-var querying or file-stat probing against credential directories across multiple cloud provider SDK paths.

suggestion.title: NadMesh Botnet C2 Communication and Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: As botnet malware, NadMesh requires command channel to receive tasking and exfiltrate stolen keys/tokens. Article focuses on credential harvesting, implying attacker collection pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for DNS requests or TLS connections to known NadMesh C2 domains (from threat feeds). Detect credential-sized data payloads in HTTP POST bodies or DNS exfiltration tunneling. Monitor for process spawning with embedded credentials or encrypted outbound beacons containing harvested key material.

suggestion.title: Detect Process Execution of Binaries Signed by Stolen DigiCert Certificates
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states certificate theft linked to GoldenEyeDog. Execution of malware signed with these certificates is the primary post-breach weaponization vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution where binary's code signature issuer is DigiCert and signing certificate serial number or thumbprint matches known-compromised set. Correlate execution timestamp, process creator, and parent process against baseline. Prioritize execution outside vendor/developer infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Issuance of Code-Signing Certificates via Compromised DigiCert Account
suggestion.rationale: Breach implies attacker access to issuance infrastructure. Monitor Certificate Transparency logs for new code-signing certificates issued post-breach with anomalous requestor patterns, geolocation, or bulk volume.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse CT logs for DigiCert-issued code-signing certificates with requestor IP geographically inconsistent with customer base, issuance outside business hours, or certificate names matching known malware families or attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Inbound Email Delivery of Code-Signed Malware
suggestion.rationale: Stolen certificates enable malware distribution disguised as legitimate signed software, bypassing reputation filters. Title explicitly links theft to GoldenEyeDog, indicating operational deployment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate email attachment hashes and signing certificates against theft advisory. Flag binaries signed by DigiCert-issued certificates on compromise list regardless of sender reputation. Capture file metadata: name, hash, signer CN, thumbprint.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Network Delivery of Code-Signed Malware
suggestion.rationale: Post-breach, attackers deploy signed malware internally via SMB, WMI, or GPO, exploiting trust in code signatures to bypass endpoint controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for binaries signed by compromised certificates created via network SMB writes, WMI file deposits, or group policy push. Flag unsigned deployments of binaries with matching code-signing certificate serial numbers in local logging.

suggestion.title: Detect Signed Malicious DLL Load via DLL Search Order Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Attackers sign malicious DLLs with stolen certificates to evade UAC/AppLocker restrictions and hijack legitimate application loading paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DLL image loads from unusual paths (temp, downloads, ProgramData) where DLL is signed with DigiCert-issued certificate on compromise list. Verify DLL load does not match application manifest or expected dependency.

suggestion.title: Detect Supply Chain Infection via Trojanized Software Update
suggestion.rationale: Stolen code-signing certificates enable repackaging of legitimate software with injected malware and re-signing, appearing legitimate during update check and distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor software update payloads (Windows Update, vendor updates) for executables signed by DigiCert certificates issued during compromise window. Cross-validate product version, signer metadata, and update timestamp against vendor release schedule. Yara scan update binaries for known malware signatures despite valid certificate chain.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox—Unauthenticated HTTP Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests' to unauthenticated FortiSandbox instances. Zero UCs generated despite this being the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FortiSandbox listening ports (typically 8080, 8443, 541) for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests with command-injection payloads (shell metacharacters: |, &, ;, `, $(). Correlate with HTTP 200/400 responses indicating processing of requests to /upload, /api, /analyze, or admin endpoints without authentication headers.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox—OS Command Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability' allowing 'unauthorized commands' execution. Missing T1059.001 (Command Line Interface) detection for actual payload execution on FortiSandbox OS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On FortiSandbox systems, detect unexpected child processes spawned from FortiSandbox service processes (fortisandbox, lighttpd, or service account runners). Look for sh/bash/cmd execution with stdin from network sockets, or process creation from HTTP service threads.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-25089—Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' using template, explicitly stating 'worth one quick check across your fleet — patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero asset-discovery detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for systems reporting FortiSandbox (any version) with CVE-2026-25089 not yet patched. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm externally-facing instances and validate patch application date against federal due date 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: Fortinet FortiSandbox Unauthenticated HTTP Command Injection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized commands via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—requires detection of malicious HTTP payloads targeting exposed FortiSandbox ports
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP POST/GET requests to FortiSandbox standard ports (4000, 4001, 5000) from external/untrusted sources containing shell metacharacters (backtick, pipe, semicolon, $(), &&, ||) or known OS command separators. Prioritize requests with error response codes indicating injection rejection.

suggestion.title: Process Spawning from FortiSandbox Service Processes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'OS command injection vulnerability'—FortiSandbox should never spawn child shells (cmd.exe, bash, sh); any such process spawning indicates exploitation of T1059.001
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by Fortinet FortiSandbox services with names: cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, sh, python.exe, or perl.exe. Inspect command line for obfuscation or encoded payloads. Match against patches issued after 2026-07-19.

suggestion.title: FortiSandbox Service Abnormal HTTP Error Patterns in Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation attempts precede successful RCE; article's federal urgency indicates defenders should hunt failed injection attempts before patch deadline
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search FortiSandbox service logs and HTTP access logs for error codes or stack traces in same timeframe as suspicious HTTP requests. Look for patterns indicating argument parsing failure, shell metacharacter rejection, or command execution errors.

suggestion.title: HTTP injection payload detection to FortiSandbox endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'via specifically crafted HTTP requests'—exploitation is HTTP-borne. Requires WAF or proxy logs for parameter inspection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to FortiSandbox with shell metacharacters, command substitution operators ($()), or OS-specific injection markers in query parameters or POST bodies. Correlate requests from external IPs to /api, /admin, or management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Command execution spawned from FortiSandbox process context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability 'allows…execution of unauthorized commands'—successful exploitation results in process creation. Look for child processes launched from FortiSandbox service account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new process creation where parent is FortiSandbox daemon (e.g., fortisandbox, fssandboxd) and child is shell, cmd.exe, powershell, or bash. Cross-reference timing with HTTP access logs for correlation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP access to FortiSandbox management interface
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated attacker'—exploitation does not require credentials. Hunt for external HTTP requests that bypass authentication checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify HTTP 200/302 responses from FortiSandbox APIs or dashboards where source IP is external and no authentication cookies/tokens are present or valid. Spike in 401→200 sequence per source IP suggests auth bypass.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability scanner match: CVE-2026-25089 on assets

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest FortiSandbox version reports from scanners and flag any instance matching vulnerable versions (versions before patched release). Cross-reference against network exposure tools to confirm external reachability.

suggestion.title: OS command stderr/stdout exfiltration from FortiSandbox
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker will want output from injected commands. Monitor FortiSandbox logs and process output for unexpected command results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag large stderr/stdout output written to unexpected file descriptors or network sockets from FortiSandbox processes. Look for base64 or hex-encoded output patterns suggesting data staging.
